+CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $HOST" "$HEALTH_URL")
+BODY=$(curl -s -H "Host: $HOST" "$HEALTH_URL")
+
+if [ "$CODE" = "200" ] && echo "$BODY" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then
+  echo "Ingress healthy"
+else
+  echo "Ingress not healthy (code=$CODE)"
+fi
+```
+
+
+## Process flows
+
+### Ingress-only quick test (recommended path)
+
+```mermaid
+sequenceDiagram
+  autonumber
+  participant Dev as make quick-load-test-ingress
+  participant SH as smoke-health
+  participant Curl as curl (IP + Host)
+  participant Nginx as NGINX Ingress
+  participant Svc as embedding-service-serve-svc
+  participant Serve as Ray Serve proxies
+  participant App as FastAPI app
+
+  Dev->>SH: Invoke smoke-health
+  SH->>Curl: GET http://<node-ip>:<node-port>/health
+  Curl->>Nginx: Host: embeddings.<ip-dashed>.nip.io
+  Nginx->>Svc: Route to service backend (8000)
+  Svc->>Serve: Forward to Serve proxy (EveryNode)
+  Serve->>App: /health
+  App-->>Serve: 200 {"status":"healthy"}
+  Serve-->>Nginx: 200
+  Nginx-->>SH: 200
+  SH-->>Dev: Health OK
+  Dev->>App: Run load_test.py to http://embeddings.<ip-dashed>.nip.io:<node-port>/embeddings
+```
+
+### Fallback logic (general quick-load-test)
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart TD
+  A[Start quick-load-test] --> B{Ingress healthy?\n(HTTP 200 + status=healthy)}
+  B -- Yes --> C[Run load_test.py to ingress URL]
+  B -- No --> D{USE_INGRESS_ONLY=true?}
+  D -- Yes --> E[Abort with message]
+  D -- No --> F[Get pod IP from embedding-service-serve-svc]
+  F --> G[Set TARGET_URL=http://<pod-ip>:8000]
+  G --> H[Run load_test.py to pod URL]
+```
+
+
+## Deep dive: Makefile architecture and variables
+
+The Makefile is organized into a few functional sections. Key variables and targets are designed to be overridden on the command line.
+
+### Core variables (override at invocation)
+
+- Kubernetes/Ray:
+  - SERVICE_NAME (default: embedding-service)
+  - RAYSERVICE_FILE (default: k8s/rayservice-local.yaml)
+  - NAMESPACE (default: default)
+- Ingress and tests:
+  - NODE_PORT (default: 30333)
+  - TEST_REQUESTS (default: 200)
+  - TEST_CONCURRENCY (default: 10)
+  - TEST_SEGMENTATION (default: false)
+  - USE_INGRESS_ONLY (default: true for ingress-only run)
+  - INGRESS_WAIT_SECS (default: 60)
+  - SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT (internal; used to bypass redundant waits in quick-load-test-ingress)
+
+Examples:
+
+```bash
+# Smaller ingress run
+make quick-load-test-ingress TEST_REQUESTS=50 TEST_CONCURRENCY=5
+
+# Heavier run with segmentation
+make quick-load-test-ingress TEST_REQUESTS=1000 TEST_CONCURRENCY=20 TEST_SEGMENTATION=true
+
+# General load test that can fall back to a pod IP
+make quick-load-test TEST_REQUESTS=200 TEST_CONCURRENCY=10 USE_INGRESS_ONLY=false INGRESS_WAIT_SECS=30
+```
+
+### Build and image variables
+
+These back the Docker build/push targets:
+
+- REGISTRY (default: 192.168.1.3:5000)
+- IMAGE_NAME (default: embedding-service)
+- VERSION_FILE (default: version)
+- VERSION (read from version file, default latest)
+- FULL_IMAGE_TAG = $(REGISTRY)/$(IMAGE_NAME):$(VERSION)
+
+Targets: version-bump, docker-build, docker-push, build-and-push-optimized.
+
+```bash
+# Build and push with version bump
+make build-and-push-optimized
+```
+
+
+## Target walkthroughs with references
+
+Below, we reference exact target names and the logic found in Makefile.
+
+### 1) redeploy-clean
+
+- Deletes the RayService and force-deletes lingering pods with label ray.io/is-ray-node=yes.
+- If nvidia-smi exists, prints GPU process table for sanity (ensures GPUs are free before a fresh rollout).
+
+### 2) deploy-apply
+
+- Applies $(RAYSERVICE_FILE) and waits for Ray pods Ready (timeout 10m).
+- Waits for Serve endpoints in $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc.
+- Prints pods with kubectl get pods -o wide for quick visibility.
+
+### 3) smoke-health
+
+- Builds HOST = embeddings.<NODE_IP dashed>.nip.io and requests http://<NODE_IP>:<NODE_PORT>/health with Host: <HOST>.
+- Pass criteria: HTTP 200 and JSON body containing "status":"healthy".
+- Falls back to a direct pod IP health check if the ingress path fails, and errors if both fail.
+
+### 4) quick-load-test-ingress
+
+- Depends on smoke-health (so ingress is validated first).
+- Computes http://embeddings.<NODE_IP dashed>.nip.io:$(NODE_PORT) and calls the Python client (working_dir/load_test.py) directly.
+- This path avoids duplicate health loops to reduce flakiness.
+
+### 5) quick-load-test
+
+- General-purpose target.
+- Optionally waits for ingress health (same contract as smoke-health).
+- If ingress isn’t healthy:
+  - With USE_INGRESS_ONLY=true it aborts early.
+  - Otherwise, it fetches a pod IP from $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc and re-targets the client to http://<pod-ip>:8000.
+
+### 6) redeploy and redeploy-and-test
+
+- redeploy: redeploy-clean → deploy-apply → smoke-health.
+- redeploy-and-test: runs redeploy, then quick-load-test (ingress preferred, with fallback depending on flags).
+
+
+## The load test client: working_dir/load_test.py
+
+The client is intentionally minimal and dependency-free, built on Python’s standard library.
+
+- Endpoint: POST /embeddings
+- Payload shape:
+
+```json
+{
+  "texts": ["...", "...", "..."],
+  "use_segmentation": true,
+  "include_segment_embeddings": false,
+  "show_progress": false
+}
+```
+
+- Concurrency: uses ThreadPoolExecutor with max_workers = TEST_CONCURRENCY.
+- Errors: HTTPError yields the HTTP status (e.g., 429, 500). Non-HTTP exceptions yield status 0.
+- Reporting: total requests, per-status distribution, mean, p50, p95, p99 based on wall-clock latencies.
+
+Excerpt:
+
+```python
+with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as ex:
+    futs = [ex.submit(post_json, url, payload) for _ in range(total)]
+    for f in as_completed(futs):
+        s, l = f.result()
+        statuses.append(s)
+        latencies.append(l)
+```
+
+
+## Health contract: detailed
+
+The service health is considered OK IFF both conditions are true:
+
+1) HTTP 200 from /health via ingress path (IP + Host header)
+2) Response body contains "status":"healthy"
+
+Why both? HTTP 200 alone can come from an upstream placeholder or default backend; the JSON body proves the request reached the application and not an error handler.
+
+Debugging tips:
+
+```bash
+# Verify Host resolution vs Node IP (informational)
+getent hosts embeddings.<ip-dashed>.nip.io
+
+# Direct health probe with ingress routing
+curl -si -H "Host: embeddings.<ip-dashed>.nip.io" \
+  http://<node-ip>:<node-port>/health
+```
+
+
+## DNS and nip.io
+
+- The Makefile probes ingress using an IP-based URL with the Host header set. This decouples test success from external DNS and still exercises NGINX vhost routing.
+- A warning is printed if getent hosts returns an IP different from the NODE_IP, but health still passes because the TCP connection goes to NODE_IP.
+
+
+## Performance methodology and tuning
+
+Where to tune:
+
+- App-level semaphores and limits: see src/config.py for embedding_concurrency_limit, similarity_concurrency_limit, and other caps.
+- Ray Serve deployment parameters: see deployment wrapper (e.g., max_ongoing_requests, autoscaling target per replica). Ensure HTTP proxies run on EveryNode.
+- Ingress warm-up: allow a short warm-up before heavy bursts. Use INGRESS_WAIT_SECS or run a small quick-load-test-ingress first.
+
+Suggested steps:
+
+1) Prove routing with R=50, C=5.
+2) Increase to R=200, C=10.
+3) For segmentation-heavy tests, adjust concurrency cautiously and watch for 429/500.
+4) Monitor p95/p99 under sustained load; consider adding autoscaling slack or lowering per-replica targets.
+
+
+## Troubleshooting cookbook
+
+Common symptoms and suggested checks:
+
+- HTTP 000 in health checks:
+  - Connection or listener issue. Confirm NodePort, NGINX status, and that nothing is blocking the port.
+  - Try curl -v with the Host header to see connection-level errors.
+
+- 503 during warm-up:
+  - Give more warm-up time; check that Serve deployments are ready.
+  - Confirm readiness probes in your RayService manifest are passing.
+
+- 429 under segmentation:
+  - Indicates capacity or rate limit thresholds. Increase app concurrency or Serve max_ongoing_requests gradually.
+
+- Ingress healthy but app errors persist:
+  - Use quick-load-test with USE_INGRESS_ONLY=false to isolate app behavior via pod IP.
+  - Inspect logs from Ray head/worker pods and NGINX controller.
+
+- DNS mismatch (nip.io vs NODE_IP):
+  - Informational only due to IP+Host probing. For public DNS, consider a stable hostname or a LoadBalancer ingress.
+
+
+## CI/CD examples
+
+You can wire a basic validation stage that fails fast on ingress health, then runs a short ingress-only load test:
+
+```bash
+make smoke-health
+make quick-load-test-ingress TEST_REQUESTS=50 TEST_CONCURRENCY=5
+```
+
+Optionally add a pod-level fallback check (do not fail the pipeline if ingress is flaky, but capture signal):
+
+```bash
+make quick-load-test TEST_REQUESTS=50 TEST_CONCURRENCY=5 USE_INGRESS_ONLY=false || true
+```
+
+You can assert on the output (e.g., grep for "non-200: 0") to enforce SLAs.
+
+
+## Appendix: Selected Makefile excerpts
+
+Health check core (appears in smoke-health):
+
+```make
+CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true)
+RES=$$(curl -s -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true)
+if [ "$$CODE" != "200" ] || ! echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then ... fi
+```
+
+Ingress-only runner (after smoke-health succeeds):
+
+```make
+@set -euo pipefail; \
+. ./.make.cached.env; \
+IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
+URL=http://$$HOST:$(NODE_PORT); \
+python3 working_dir/load_test.py --url $$URL \
+  --requests $(TEST_REQUESTS) --concurrency $(TEST_CONCURRENCY) \
+  --segmentation $(TEST_SEGMENTATION)
+```
+
+General quick-load-test fallback (pod IP path):
+
+```make
+POD_IP=$$(kubectl get endpoints $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}')
+TARGET_URL=http://$$POD_IP:8000
+python3 working_dir/load_test.py --url $$TARGET_URL \
+  --requests $(TEST_REQUESTS) --concurrency $(TEST_CONCURRENCY) \
+  --segmentation $(TEST_SEGMENTATION)
+```
+
+
+## Variable cheat sheet
+
+- NODE_PORT: Ingress HTTP port (NodePort)
+- TEST_REQUESTS: Total number of requests
+- TEST_CONCURRENCY: Number of worker threads in the client
+- TEST_SEGMENTATION: Toggle segmentation workload (true/false)
+- USE_INGRESS_ONLY: Abort if ingress isn’t healthy (used by quick-load-test)
+- INGRESS_WAIT_SECS: Max wait for ingress health
+- SERVICE_NAME, NAMESPACE, RAYSERVICE_FILE: Kubernetes/Ray deployment parameters
+
+
+---
+
+With this flow, ingress health and load testing use the same contract (HTTP 200 + {"status":"healthy"}), removing inconsistent outcomes and making test runs reliable and reproducible. # Makefile test and optimisation guide This guide explains how the Makefile drives deploy, health checks, and load tests for the Embedding Service, and how to tune workflows for reliable, repeatable ingress tests. It includes process diagrams, code snippets, and troubleshooting tips. ## Overview Key targets referenced in this guide: - smoke-health: Probes the service via NGINX Ingress using an IP-based connection and Host routing, and validates both HTTP status and JSON body. - quick-load-test-ingress: Preferred. Runs a load test strictly through ingress after smoke-health passes. - quick-load-test: Flexible. Prefers ingress but can fall back to a pod IP if allowed. - redeploy, redeploy-and-test: Automate cleanup, apply manifests, verify health, and optionally run a quick test. ## Health check design To avoid DNS flakiness while still exercising Ingress routing rules, the health checks: - Connect to the Node IP on the NodePort - Send the Host: embeddings..nip.io header - Require HTTP 200 and a JSON body reporting {"status":"healthy"} This ensures the request enters NGINX via the correct vhost while avoiding unpredictable nip.io DNS resolution at curl time. ### Health check snippet ```bash # Pseudocode excerpt used by smoke-health and internal waits HOST="embeddings.${NODE_IP//./-}.nip.io" HEALTH_URL="http://${NODE_IP}:${NODE_PORT}/health" CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $HOST" "$HEALTH_URL") BODY=$(curl -s -H "Host: $HOST" "$HEALTH_URL") if [ "$CODE" = "200" ] && echo "$BODY" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then echo "Ingress healthy" else echo "Ingress not healthy (code=$CODE)" fi ``` ## Process flows ### Ingress-only quick test (recommended path) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant Dev as make quick-load-test-ingress participant SH as smoke-health participant Curl as curl (IP + Host) participant Nginx as NGINX Ingress participant Svc as embedding-service-serve-svc participant Serve as Ray Serve proxies participant App as FastAPI app Dev->>SH: Invoke smoke-health SH->>Curl: GET http://:/health Curl->>Nginx: Host: embeddings..nip.io Nginx->>Svc: Route to service backend (8000) Svc->>Serve: Forward to Serve proxy (EveryNode) Serve->>App: /health App-->>Serve: 200 {"status":"healthy"} Serve-->>Nginx: 200 Nginx-->>SH: 200 SH-->>Dev: Health OK Dev->>App: Run load_test.py to http://embeddings..nip.io:/embeddings ``` ### Fallback logic (general quick-load-test) ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Start quick-load-test] --> B{Ingress healthy?
HTTP 200 and status healthy} B -- Yes --> C[Run load_test.py to ingress URL] B -- No --> D{USE_INGRESS_ONLY=true?} D -- Yes --> E[Abort with message] D -- No --> F[Get pod IP from embedding-service-serve-svc] F --> G[Set TARGET_URL=http://:8000] G --> H[Run load_test.py to pod URL] ``` ## Deep dive: Makefile architecture and variables The Makefile is organized into a few functional sections. Key variables and targets are designed to be overridden on the command line. ### Core variables (override at invocation) - Kubernetes/Ray: - SERVICE_NAME (default: embedding-service) - RAYSERVICE_FILE (default: k8s/rayservice-local.yaml) - NAMESPACE (default: default) - Ingress and tests: - NODE_PORT (default: 30333) - TEST_REQUESTS (default: 200) - TEST_CONCURRENCY (default: 10) - TEST_SEGMENTATION (default: false) - USE_INGRESS_ONLY (default: true for ingress-only run) - INGRESS_WAIT_SECS (default: 60) - SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT (internal; used to bypass redundant waits in quick-load-test-ingress) Examples: ```bash # Smaller ingress run make quick-load-test-ingress TEST_REQUESTS=50 TEST_CONCURRENCY=5 # Heavier run with segmentation make quick-load-test-ingress TEST_REQUESTS=1000 TEST_CONCURRENCY=20 TEST_SEGMENTATION=true # General load test that can fall back to a pod IP make quick-load-test TEST_REQUESTS=200 TEST_CONCURRENCY=10 USE_INGRESS_ONLY=false INGRESS_WAIT_SECS=30 ``` ### Build and image variables These back the Docker build/push targets: - REGISTRY (default: 192.168.1.3:5000) - IMAGE_NAME (default: embedding-service) - VERSION_FILE (default: version) - VERSION (read from version file, default latest) - FULL_IMAGE_TAG = $(REGISTRY)/$(IMAGE_NAME):$(VERSION) Targets: version-bump, docker-build, docker-push, build-and-push-optimized. ```bash # Build and push with version bump make build-and-push-optimized ``` ## Target walkthroughs with references Below, we reference exact target names and the logic found in Makefile. ### 1) redeploy-clean - Deletes the RayService and force-deletes lingering pods with label ray.io/is-ray-node=yes. - If nvidia-smi exists, prints GPU process table for sanity (ensures GPUs are free before a fresh rollout). ### 2) deploy-apply - Applies $(RAYSERVICE_FILE) and waits for Ray pods Ready (timeout 10m). - Waits for Serve endpoints in $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc. - Prints pods with kubectl get pods -o wide for quick visibility. ### 3) smoke-health - Builds HOST = embeddings..nip.io and requests http://:/health with Host: . - Pass criteria: HTTP 200 and JSON body containing "status":"healthy". - Falls back to a direct pod IP health check if the ingress path fails, and errors if both fail. ### 4) quick-load-test-ingress - Depends on smoke-health (so ingress is validated first). - Computes http://embeddings..nip.io:$(NODE_PORT) and calls the Python client (working_dir/load_test.py) directly. - This path avoids duplicate health loops to reduce flakiness. ### 5) quick-load-test - General-purpose target. - Optionally waits for ingress health (same contract as smoke-health). - If ingress isn’t healthy: - With USE_INGRESS_ONLY=true it aborts early. - Otherwise, it fetches a pod IP from $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc and re-targets the client to http://:8000. ### 6) redeploy and redeploy-and-test - redeploy: redeploy-clean → deploy-apply → smoke-health. - redeploy-and-test: runs redeploy, then quick-load-test (ingress preferred, with fallback depending on flags). ## The load test client: working_dir/load_test.py The client is intentionally minimal and dependency-free, built on Python’s standard library. - Endpoint: POST /embeddings - Payload shape: ```json { "texts": ["...", "...", "..."], "use_segmentation": true, "include_segment_embeddings": false, "show_progress": false } ``` - Concurrency: uses ThreadPoolExecutor with max_workers = TEST_CONCURRENCY. - Errors: HTTPError yields the HTTP status (e.g., 429, 500). Non-HTTP exceptions yield status 0. - Reporting: total requests, per-status distribution, mean, p50, p95, p99 based on wall-clock latencies. HTTP 200 alone can come from an upstream placeholder or default backend; the JSON body proves the request reached the application and not an error handler. Debugging tips: ```bash # Verify Host resolution vs Node IP (informational) getent hosts embeddings..nip.io # Direct health probe with ingress routing curl -si -H "Host: embeddings..nip.io" \ http://:/health ``` ## DNS and nip.io - The Makefile probes ingress using an IP-based URL with the Host header set. This decouples test success from external DNS and still exercises NGINX vhost routing. - A warning is printed if getent hosts returns an IP different from the NODE_IP, but health still passes because the TCP connection goes to NODE_IP. ## Performance methodology and tuning Where to tune: - App-level semaphores and limits: see src/config.py for embedding_concurrency_limit, similarity_concurrency_limit, and other caps. - Ray Serve deployment parameters: see deployment wrapper (e.g., max_ongoing_requests, autoscaling target per replica). Ensure HTTP proxies run on EveryNode. - Ingress warm-up: allow a short warm-up before heavy bursts. Use INGRESS_WAIT_SECS or run a small quick-load-test-ingress first. Suggested steps: 1) Prove routing with R=50, C=5. 2) Increase to R=200, C=10. 3) For segmentation-heavy tests, adjust concurrency cautiously and watch for 429/500. 4) Monitor p95/p99 under sustained load; consider adding autoscaling slack or lowering per-replica targets. ## Troubleshooting cookbook Common symptoms and suggested checks: - HTTP 000 in health checks: - Connection or listener issue. Confirm NodePort, NGINX status, and that nothing is blocking the port. - Try curl -v with the Host header to see connection-level errors. - 503 during warm-up: - Give more warm-up time; check that Serve deployments are ready. - Confirm readiness probes in your RayService manifest are passing. - 429 under segmentation: - Indicates capacity or rate limit thresholds. Increase app concurrency or Serve max_ongoing_requests gradually. - Ingress healthy but app errors persist: - Use quick-load-test with USE_INGRESS_ONLY=false to isolate app behavior via pod IP. - Inspect logs from Ray head/worker pods and NGINX controller. - DNS mismatch (nip.io vs NODE_IP): - Informational only due to IP+Host probing. SHELL := /bin/bash
VIRTUALENV_NAME := $(shell basename $(CURDIR))

PIP_COMPILE_ARGS = -v -U --no-emit-index-url --no-emit-trusted-host --strip-extras --resolver=backtracking

PYTHON_VERSION = 3.12.1 # keep minor versions syncd

# Colors for output
RED := \033[0;31m
GREEN := \033[0;32m
YELLOW := \033[0;33m
BLUE := \033[0;34m
BOLD := \033[1m
RESET := \033[0m


.PHONY: _python_version
_python_version:
	@if [ -z $(PYTHON_VERSION) ]; then \
		echo "$(RED)$(BOLD)This is the python verion $(PYTHON_VERSION)$(RESET)"; \
		exit 1; \
	fi


.PHONY: pyenv
pyenv: | _python_version # create a python virtual env
	@echo "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)Creating a virtual environment$(RESET)"
	@if ! pyenv versions --bare | grep -q $(PYTHON_VERSION); then \
		echo "Python version $(PYTHON_VERSION) is not installed."; \
		echo "Installing this version of Python..."; \
		pyenv install -s $(PYTHON_VERSION); \
	fi
	@if ! pyenv versions --bare | grep -q $(VIRTUALENV_NAME); then \
		pyenv virtualenv $(PYTHON_VERSION) $(VIRTUALENV_NAME); else \
		echo "Virtual environment $(VIRTUALENV_NAME) already exists."; \
	fi
	@pyenv local $(VIRTUALENV_NAME)
	@pip install --upgrade pip


.PHONY: pre-commit
pre-commit:
	@pip install -q pre-commit
	@pre-commit install


.PHONY: check
check: | pre-commit
	@echo "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)Running checks (pre-commit)$(RESET)"
	pre-commit run --all-files


.PHONY: pip-tools
pip-tools:
	@echo "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)Installing pip-tools (pre-commit)$(RESET)"
	@pip install -q pip-tools


%.txt: %.in | pip-tools # Compile specified requirements (pip-compile).
	@echo "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)Compiling $*.txt$(RESET)"
	CUSTOM_COMPILE_COMMAND="make update" pip-compile $(PIP_COMPILE_ARGS) $*.in


.PHONY: requirements
requirements: requirements.in dev-requirements.in | pip-tools
	@echo "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)Compiling requirements$(RESET)"
	CUSTOM_COMPILE_COMMAND="make update" pip-compile $(PIP_COMPILE_ARGS) requirements.in --output-file requirements.txt
	CUSTOM_COMPILE_COMMAND="make update" pip-compile $(PIP_COMPILE_ARGS) dev-requirements.in --output-file dev-requirements.txt


.PHONY: sync
sync: requirements.txt dev-requirements.txt | pip-tools
	@echo "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)Syncing dependencies$(RESET)"
	pip-sync requirements.txt dev-requirements.txt


.PHONY: install
install: requirements.txt dev-requirements.txt
	@echo "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)Installing dependencies$(RESET)"
	pip install \
	-r requirements.txt -r dev-requirements.txt

.PHONY: test
test: | install

	pytest


# Docker configuration
REGISTRY ?= 192.168.1.3:5000
IMAGE_NAME ?= embedding-service
VERSION_FILE ?= version
VERSION ?= $(shell cat $(VERSION_FILE) 2>/dev/null || echo "latest")
FULL_IMAGE_TAG = $(REGISTRY)/$(IMAGE_NAME):$(VERSION)


.PHONY: version-bump
version-bump:
	@echo "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)Bumping version$(RESET)"
	@if [ -f "$(VERSION_FILE)" ]; then \
		current_version=$$(cat $(VERSION_FILE)); \
		echo "Current version: $$current_version"; \
		echo "v4.0.2" > $(VERSION_FILE); \
		echo "New version: $$(cat $(VERSION_FILE))"; \
	else \
		echo "v4.0.2" > $(VERSION_FILE); \
		echo "Created version file with: $$(cat $(VERSION_FILE))"; \
	fi


.PHONY: docker-build
docker-build:
	@echo "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)Building Docker image: $(FULL_IMAGE_TAG)$(RESET)"
	docker build -t $(FULL_IMAGE_TAG) .
	docker tag $(FULL_IMAGE_TAG) $(REGISTRY)/$(IMAGE_NAME):latest


.PHONY: docker-push
docker-push:
	@echo "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)Pushing Docker image: $(FULL_IMAGE_TAG)$(RESET)"
	docker push $(FULL_IMAGE_TAG)
	docker push $(REGISTRY)/$(IMAGE_NAME):latest


.PHONY: build-and-push-optimized
build-and-push-optimized: version-bump docker-build docker-push
	@echo "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)Successfully built and pushed optimized image: $(FULL_IMAGE_TAG)$(RESET)"


.PHONY: docker-info
docker-info:
	@echo "Registry: $(REGISTRY)"
	@echo "Image Name: $(IMAGE_NAME)"
	@echo "Version: $(VERSION)"
	@echo "Full Tag: $(FULL_IMAGE_TAG)"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Kubernetes/RayService deploy + test helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Ray/K8s variables (override at invocation if needed)
SERVICE_NAME ?= embedding-service
RAYSERVICE_FILE ?= k8s/rayservice-local.yaml
NAMESPACE ?= default

# Ingress testing vars
# If NODE_IP is not provided, we'll try to detect it at runtime
NODE_PORT ?= 30333
TEST_REQUESTS ?= 200
TEST_CONCURRENCY ?= 10
TEST_SEGMENTATION ?= false
USE_INGRESS_ONLY ?= true
INGRESS_WAIT_SECS ?= 60

.PHONY: _ensure-tools
_ensure-tools:
	@command -v kubectl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "kubectl not found in PATH"; exit 1; }
	@command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "curl not found in PATH"; exit 1; }
	@command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "python3 not found in PATH"; exit 1; }

# Ray dashboard port-forward settings
DASHBOARD_PORT ?= 8265
DASHBOARD_PID_FILE ?= run/dashboard_pf.pid

.PHONY: port-forward-dashboard
port-forward-dashboard: _ensure-tools
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Starting port-forward to Ray Dashboard on port $(DASHBOARD_PORT)$(RESET)"; \
	# Ensure run/ and logs/ directories exist
	mkdir -p run logs; \
	# Check if a previous port-forward is running
	if [ -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" ]; then \
	  OLD_PID=$$(cat "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" 2>/dev/null || true); \
	  if [ -n "$$OLD_PID" ] && ps -p "$$OLD_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Existing port-forward detected (PID=$$OLD_PID). Leaving it running.$(RESET)"; \
	    exit 0; \
	  fi; \
	fi; \
	# Locate the Ray head pod
	HEAD_POD=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/node-type=head -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
	if [ -z "$$HEAD_POD" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Could not find Ray head pod in namespace $(NAMESPACE)$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 1; \
	fi; \
	# Start port-forward in background with nohup
	LOG_FILE=logs/portforward-dashboard-$(DASHBOARD_PORT).log; \
	nohup kubectl -n $(NAMESPACE) port-forward pod/$$HEAD_POD $(DASHBOARD_PORT):$(DASHBOARD_PORT) --address 0.0.0.0 > "$$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 & \
	PF_PID=$$!; \
	echo "$$PF_PID" > "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	sleep 1; \
	if ps -p "$$PF_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward running (PID=$$PF_PID). Logs: $$LOG_FILE$(RESET)"; \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Access the dashboard at: http://127.0.0.1:$(DASHBOARD_PORT) or your host IP$(RESET)"; \
	else \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward failed to start. See $$LOG_FILE$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 1; \
	fi

.PHONY: port-forward-dashboard-stop
port-forward-dashboard-stop:
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	if [ ! -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] No PID file found (nothing to stop)$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 0; \
	fi; \
	PID=$$(cat "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" 2>/dev/null || true); \
	if [ -z "$$PID" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] PID file empty (nothing to stop)$(RESET)"; \
	  rm -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	  exit 0; \
	fi; \
	if ps -p "$$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Stopping port-forward (PID=$$PID)$(RESET)"; \
	  kill "$$PID" || true; \
	  sleep 1; \
	  if ps -p "$$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Force killing PID $$PID$(RESET)"; \
	    kill -9 "$$PID" || true; \
	  fi; \
	else \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] No running process for PID $$PID$(RESET)"; \
	fi; \
	rm -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward stopped$(RESET)"

.PHONY: _detect-node-ip
_detect-node-ip:
	@if [ -z "$(NODE_IP)" ]; then \
	  DETECTED_IP=$$(ip route get 1.1.1.1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($$i=="src") {print $$(i+1); exit}}'); \
	  if [ -z "$$DETECTED_IP" ]; then \
	    echo "$(RED)$(BOLD)Unable to auto-detect NODE_IP; please pass NODE_IP=...$(RESET)"; \
	    exit 1; \
	  fi; \
	  echo "Using auto-detected NODE_IP=$$DETECTED_IP"; \
	  echo "NODE_IP=$$DETECTED_IP" > .make.cached.env; \
	else \
	  echo "NODE_IP=$(NODE_IP)" > .make.cached.env; \
	fi

.PHONY: redeploy-clean
redeploy-clean: _ensure-tools
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Deleting RayService $(SERVICE_NAME)$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl delete rayservice $(SERVICE_NAME) -n $(NAMESPACE) --ignore-not-found=true || true; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Waiting briefly for pods to terminate$(RESET)"; \
	sleep 3; \
	PODS=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes -o name 2>/dev/null || true); \
		if [ -n "$$PODS" ]; then \
			printf "%b\n" "Found lingering Ray pods, forcing deletion:"; printf "%b\n" "$$PODS"; \
	  kubectl delete $$PODS -n $(NAMESPACE) --force --grace-period=0 || true; \
	fi; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Verifying no Ray pods remain$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes || true; \
	if command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Checking GPU processes$(RESET)"; \
	  nvidia-smi || true; \
	fi

.PHONY: deploy-apply
deploy-apply: _ensure-tools
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Applying $(RAYSERVICE_FILE)$(RESET)"; \
		kubectl apply -n $(NAMESPACE) -f $(RAYSERVICE_FILE); \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Waiting for Ray pods to appear$(RESET)"; \
	for i in $$(seq 1 60); do \
	  CNT=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes -o name 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '); \
			if [ "$$CNT" -gt 0 ]; then printf "%b\n" "Found $$CNT Ray pods"; break; fi; \
	  sleep 2; \
	done; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Waiting for Ray pods Ready (timeout 10m)$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl wait --for=condition=ready pod -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes --timeout=600s; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Waiting for Serve endpoints to be ready$(RESET)"; \
	for i in $$(seq 1 150); do \
	  EP=$$(kubectl get endpoints $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[*].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
			if [ -n "$$EP" ]; then printf "%b\n" "Serve endpoints: $$EP"; break; fi; \
	  sleep 2; \
	done; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Ray pods Ready$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -o wide | sed -n '1,200p'

.PHONY: smoke-health
smoke-health: _ensure-tools _detect-node-ip
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		. ./.make.cached.env; \
		IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
		ENDPOINT_IP=http://$${NODE_IP}:$(NODE_PORT); \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Checking health via Ingress: $$ENDPOINT_IP/health (Host: $$HOST)$(RESET)"; \
		RESOLVE=$$(getent hosts $$HOST 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $$1}' | head -n1 || true); \
		if [ -n "$$RESOLVE" ] && [ "$$RESOLVE" != "$$NODE_IP" ]; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Warning: $$HOST resolves to $$RESOLVE, expected $$NODE_IP$(RESET)"; \
		fi; \
		CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
		RES=$$(curl -s -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
		printf "%b\n" "Health code: $$CODE body: $$RES"; \
		if [ "$$CODE" != "200" ] || ! echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Ingress not healthy (code=$$CODE), trying direct pod endpoint fallback$(RESET)"; \
			POD_IP=$$(kubectl get endpoints embedding-service-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
			if [ -n "$$POD_IP" ]; then \
				printf "%b\n" "Trying http://$$POD_IP:8000/health"; \
				CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://$$POD_IP:8000/health || true); \
				RES=$$(curl -s http://$$POD_IP:8000/health || true); \
				printf "%b\n" "Fallback code: $$CODE body: $$RES"; \
				if [ "$$CODE" != "200" ] || ! echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then \
					printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Fallback health also not healthy$(RESET)"; \
					exit 1; \
				fi; \
			else \
				printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Could not determine pod IP for fallback$(RESET)"; \
				exit 1; \
			fi; \
		fi; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Health OK$(RESET)"

.PHONY: quick-load-test
quick-load-test: _ensure-tools _detect-node-ip
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		. ./.make.cached.env; \
		IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
	TARGET_URL=http://$$HOST:$(NODE_PORT); \
	HEALTH_URL=http://$${NODE_IP}:$(NODE_PORT); \
	printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Debug: HOST=$$HOST TARGET_URL=$$TARGET_URL HEALTH_URL=$$HEALTH_URL$(RESET)"; \
	# Prefer ingress: health wait (skip if SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT=true)
	if [ "$${SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT:-false}" != "true" ]; then \
	  START=$$(date +%s); \
	  OK=false; \
	  while :; do \
	    CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$HEALTH_URL/health || true); \
	    RES=$$(curl -s -H "Host: $$HOST" $$HEALTH_URL/health || true); \
	    if [ "$$CODE" = "200" ] && echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then OK=true; break; fi; \
	    NOW=$$(date +%s); \
	    ELAPSED=$$((NOW-START)); \
	    if [ "$$ELAPSED" -ge "$(INGRESS_WAIT_SECS)" ]; then break; fi; \
	    sleep 2; \
	  done; \
	  if [ "$$OK" != "true" ]; then \
	    if [ "$(USE_INGRESS_ONLY)" = "true" ]; then \
	      printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Ingress not healthy after $(INGRESS_WAIT_SECS)s (last code=$$CODE). Aborting per USE_INGRESS_ONLY=true$(RESET)"; \
	      exit 1; \
	    else \
	      POD_IP=$$(kubectl get endpoints $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
	      if [ -n "$$POD_IP" ]; then \
	        TARGET_URL=http://$$POD_IP:8000; \
	        printf "%b\n" "Ingress not ready (last code=$$CODE), falling back to direct pod URL: $$TARGET_URL"; \
	      fi; \
	    fi; \
	  fi; \
	fi; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Running load test to $$TARGET_URL: R=$(TEST_REQUESTS) C=$(TEST_CONCURRENCY) segmentation=$(TEST_SEGMENTATION)$(RESET)"; \
	python3 working_dir/load_test.py --url $$TARGET_URL --requests $(TEST_REQUESTS) --concurrency $(TEST_CONCURRENCY) --segmentation $(TEST_SEGMENTATION)

.PHONY: quick-load-test-ingress
quick-load-test-ingress: smoke-health
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	. ./.make.cached.env; \
	IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
	URL=http://$$HOST:$(NODE_PORT); \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test-ingress] Running ingress-only load test: $$URL R=$(TEST_REQUESTS) C=$(TEST_CONCURRENCY) segmentation=$(TEST_SEGMENTATION)$(RESET)"; \
	python3 working_dir/load_test.py --url $$URL --requests $(TEST_REQUESTS) --concurrency $(TEST_CONCURRENCY) --segmentation $(TEST_SEGMENTATION)

.PHONY: redeploy
redeploy: redeploy-clean deploy-apply smoke-health
	@printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[redeploy] Completed cleanup, deploy, and health verification$(RESET)"

.PHONY: redeploy-and-test
redeploy-and-test: redeploy quick-load-test
	@printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[redeploy-and-test] Completed end-to-end redeploy with load test$(RESET)"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Kubernetes/RayService deploy + test helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Ray/K8s variables (override at invocation if needed)
SERVICE_NAME ?= embedding-service
RAYSERVICE_FILE ?= k8s/rayservice-local.yaml
NAMESPACE ?= default

# Ingress testing vars
# If NODE_IP is not provided, we'll try to detect it at runtime
NODE_PORT ?= 30333
TEST_REQUESTS ?= 200
TEST_CONCURRENCY ?= 10
TEST_SEGMENTATION ?= false
USE_INGRESS_ONLY ?= true
INGRESS_WAIT_SECS ?= 60

.PHONY: _ensure-tools
_ensure-tools:
	@command -v kubectl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "kubectl not found in PATH"; exit 1; }
	@command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "curl not found in PATH"; exit 1; }
	@command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "python3 not found in PATH"; exit 1; }

# Ray dashboard port-forward settings
DASHBOARD_PORT ?= 8265
DASHBOARD_PID_FILE ?= run/dashboard_pf.pid

.PHONY: port-forward-dashboard
port-forward-dashboard: _ensure-tools
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Starting port-forward to Ray Dashboard on port $(DASHBOARD_PORT)$(RESET)"; \
	# Ensure run/ and logs/ directories exist
	mkdir -p run logs; \
	# Check if a previous port-forward is running
	if [ -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" ]; then \
	  OLD_PID=$$(cat "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" 2>/dev/null || true); \
	  if [ -n "$$OLD_PID" ] && ps -p "$$OLD_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Existing port-forward detected (PID=$$OLD_PID). Leaving it running.$(RESET)"; \
	    exit 0; \
	  fi; \
	fi; \
	# Locate the Ray head pod
	HEAD_POD=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/node-type=head -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
	if [ -z "$$HEAD_POD" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Could not find Ray head pod in namespace $(NAMESPACE)$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 1; \
	fi; \
	# Start port-forward in background with nohup
	LOG_FILE=logs/portforward-dashboard-$(DASHBOARD_PORT).log; \
	nohup kubectl -n $(NAMESPACE) port-forward pod "$$HEAD_POD" $(DASHBOARD_PORT):$(DASHBOARD_PORT) --address 0.0.0.0 > "$$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 & \
	PF_PID=$$!; \
	echo "$$PF_PID" > "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	sleep 1; \
	if ps -p "$$PF_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward running (PID=$$PF_PID). Logs: $$LOG_FILE$(RESET)"; \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Access the dashboard at: http://127.0.0.1:$(DASHBOARD_PORT) or your host IP$(RESET)"; \
	else \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward failed to start. See $$LOG_FILE$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 1; \
	fi

.PHONY: port-forward-dashboard-stop
port-forward-dashboard-stop:
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	if [ ! -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] No PID file found (nothing to stop)$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 0; \
	fi; \
	PID=$$(cat "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" 2>/dev/null || true); \
	if [ -z "$$PID" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] PID file empty (nothing to stop)$(RESET)"; \
	  rm -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	  exit 0; \
	fi; \
	if ps -p "$$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Stopping port-forward (PID=$$PID)$(RESET)"; \
	  kill "$$PID" || true; \
	  sleep 1; \
	  if ps -p "$$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Force killing PID $$PID$(RESET)"; \
	    kill -9 "$$PID" || true; \
	  fi; \
	else \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] No running process for PID $$PID$(RESET)"; \
	fi; \
	rm -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward stopped$(RESET)"

.PHONY: _detect-node-ip
_detect-node-ip:
	@if [ -z "$(NODE_IP)" ]; then \
	  DETECTED_IP=$$(ip route get 1.1.1.1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($$i=="src") {print $$(i+1); exit}}'); \
	  if [ -z "$$DETECTED_IP" ]; then \
	    echo "$(RED)$(BOLD)Unable to auto-detect NODE_IP; please pass NODE_IP=...$(RESET)"; \
	    exit 1; \
	  fi; \
	  echo "Using auto-detected NODE_IP=$$DETECTED_IP"; \
	  echo "NODE_IP=$$DETECTED_IP" > .make.cached.env; \
	else \
	  echo "NODE_IP=$(NODE_IP)" > .make.cached.env; \
	fi

.PHONY: redeploy-clean
redeploy-clean: _ensure-tools
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Deleting RayService $(SERVICE_NAME)$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl delete rayservice $(SERVICE_NAME) -n $(NAMESPACE) --ignore-not-found=true || true; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Waiting briefly for pods to terminate$(RESET)"; \
	sleep 3; \
	PODS=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes -o name 2>/dev/null || true); \
		if [ -n "$$PODS" ]; then \
			printf "%b\n" "Found lingering Ray pods, forcing deletion:"; printf "%b\n" "$$PODS"; \
	  kubectl delete $$PODS -n $(NAMESPACE) --force --grace-period=0 || true; \
	fi; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Verifying no Ray pods remain$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes || true; \
	if command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Checking GPU processes$(RESET)"; \
	  nvidia-smi || true; \
	fi

.PHONY: deploy-apply
deploy-apply: _ensure-tools
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Applying $(RAYSERVICE_FILE)$(RESET)"; \
		kubectl apply -n $(NAMESPACE) -f $(RAYSERVICE_FILE); \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Waiting for Ray pods to appear$(RESET)"; \
	for i in $$(seq 1 60); do \
	  CNT=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes -o name 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '); \
			if [ "$$CNT" -gt 0 ]; then printf "%b\n" "Found $$CNT Ray pods"; break; fi; \
	  sleep 2; \
	done; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Waiting for Ray pods Ready (timeout 10m)$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl wait --for=condition=ready pod -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes --timeout=600s; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Waiting for Serve endpoints to be ready$(RESET)"; \
	for i in $$(seq 1 150); do \
	  EP=$$(kubectl get endpoints $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[*].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
			if [ -n "$$EP" ]; then printf "%b\n" "Serve endpoints: $$EP"; break; fi; \
	  sleep 2; \
	done; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Ray pods Ready$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -o wide | sed -n '1,200p'

.PHONY: smoke-health
smoke-health: _ensure-tools _detect-node-ip
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		. ./.make.cached.env; \
		IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
		ENDPOINT_IP=http://$${NODE_IP}:$(NODE_PORT); \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Checking health via Ingress: $$ENDPOINT_IP/health (Host: $$HOST)$(RESET)"; \
		RESOLVE=$$(getent hosts $$HOST 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $$1}' | head -n1 || true); \
		if [ -n "$$RESOLVE" ] && [ "$$RESOLVE" != "$$NODE_IP" ]; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Warning: $$HOST resolves to $$RESOLVE, expected $$NODE_IP$(RESET)"; \
		fi; \
		CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
		RES=$$(curl -s -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
		printf "%b\n" "Health code: $$CODE body: $$RES"; \
		if [ "$$CODE" != "200" ] || ! echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Ingress not healthy (code=$$CODE), trying direct pod endpoint fallback$(RESET)"; \
			POD_IP=$$(kubectl get endpoints embedding-service-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
			if [ -n "$$POD_IP" ]; then \
				printf "%b\n" "Trying http://$$POD_IP:8000/health"; \
				CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://$$POD_IP:8000/health || true); \
				RES=$$(curl -s http://$$POD_IP:8000/health || true); \
				printf "%b\n" "Fallback code: $$CODE body: $$RES"; \
				if [ "$$CODE" != "200" ] || ! echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then \
					printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Fallback health also not healthy$(RESET)"; \
					exit 1; \
				fi; \
			else \
				printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Could not determine pod IP for fallback$(RESET)"; \
				exit 1; \
			fi; \
		fi; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Health OK$(RESET)"

.PHONY: quick-load-test
quick-load-test: _ensure-tools _detect-node-ip
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		. ./.make.cached.env; \
		IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
	TARGET_URL=http://$$HOST:$(NODE_PORT); \
	HEALTH_URL=http://$${NODE_IP}:$(NODE_PORT); \
	printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Debug: HOST=$$HOST TARGET_URL=$$TARGET_URL HEALTH_URL=$$HEALTH_URL$(RESET)"; \
	# Prefer ingress: health wait (skip if SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT=true)
	if [ "$${SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT:-false}" != "true" ]; then \
	  START=$$(date +%s); \
	  OK=false; \
	  while :; do \
	    CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$HEALTH_URL/health || true); \
	    RES=$$(curl -s -H "Host: $$HOST" $$HEALTH_URL/health || true); \
	    if [ "$$CODE" = "200" ] && echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then OK=true; break; fi; \
	    NOW=$$(date +%s); \
	    ELAPSED=$$((NOW-START)); \
	    if [ "$$ELAPSED" -ge "$(INGRESS_WAIT_SECS)" ]; then break; fi; \
	    sleep 2; \
	  done; \
	  if [ "$$OK" != "true" ]; then \
	    if [ "$(USE_INGRESS_ONLY)" = "true" ]; then \
	      printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Ingress not healthy after $(INGRESS_WAIT_SECS)s (last code=$$CODE). Aborting per USE_INGRESS_ONLY=true$(RESET)"; \
	      exit 1; \
	    else \
	      POD_IP=$$(kubectl get endpoints $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
	      if [ -n "$$POD_IP" ]; then \
	        TARGET_URL=http://$$POD_IP:8000; \
	        printf "%b\n" "Ingress not ready (last code=$$CODE), falling back to direct pod URL: $$TARGET_URL"; \
	      fi; \
	    fi; \
	  fi; \
	fi; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Running load test to $$TARGET_URL: R=$(TEST_REQUESTS) C=$(TEST_CONCURRENCY) segmentation=$(TEST_SEGMENTATION)$(RESET)"; \
	python3 working_dir/load_test.py --url $$TARGET_URL --requests $(TEST_REQUESTS) --concurrency $(TEST_CONCURRENCY) --segmentation $(TEST_SEGMENTATION)

.PHONY: quick-load-test-ingress
quick-load-test-ingress: smoke-health
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	. ./.make.cached.env; \
	IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
	URL=http://$$HOST:$(NODE_PORT); \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test-ingress] Running ingress-only load test: $$URL R=$(TEST_REQUESTS) C=$(TEST_CONCURRENCY) segmentation=$(TEST_SEGMENTATION)$(RESET)"; \
	python3 working_dir/load_test.py --url $$URL --requests $(TEST_REQUESTS) --concurrency $(TEST_CONCURRENCY) --segmentation $(TEST_SEGMENTATION)

.PHONY: redeploy
redeploy: redeploy-clean deploy-apply smoke-health
	@printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[redeploy] Completed cleanup, deploy, and health verification$(RESET)"

.PHONY: redeploy-and-test
redeploy-and-test: redeploy quick-load-test
	@printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[redeploy-and-test] Completed end-to-end redeploy with load test$(RESET)"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Kubernetes/RayService deploy + test helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Ray/K8s variables (override at invocation if needed)
SERVICE_NAME ?= embedding-service
RAYSERVICE_FILE ?= k8s/rayservice-local.yaml
NAMESPACE ?= default

# Ingress testing vars
# If NODE_IP is not provided, we'll try to detect it at runtime
NODE_PORT ?= 30333
TEST_REQUESTS ?= 200
TEST_CONCURRENCY ?= 10
TEST_SEGMENTATION ?= false
USE_INGRESS_ONLY ?= true
INGRESS_WAIT_SECS ?= 60

.PHONY: _ensure-tools
_ensure-tools:
	@command -v kubectl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "kubectl not found in PATH"; exit 1; }
	@command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "curl not found in PATH"; exit 1; }
	@command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "python3 not found in PATH"; exit 1; }

# Ray dashboard port-forward settings
DASHBOARD_PORT ?= 8265
DASHBOARD_PID_FILE ?= run/dashboard_pf.pid

.PHONY: port-forward-dashboard
port-forward-dashboard: _ensure-tools
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Starting port-forward to Ray Dashboard on port $(DASHBOARD_PORT)$(RESET)"; \
	# Ensure run/ and logs/ directories exist
	mkdir -p run logs; \
	# Check if a previous port-forward is running
	if [ -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" ]; then \
	  OLD_PID=$$(cat "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" 2>/dev/null || true); \
	  if [ -n "$$OLD_PID" ] && ps -p "$$OLD_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Existing port-forward detected (PID=$$OLD_PID). Leaving it running.$(RESET)"; \
	    exit 0; \
	  fi; \
	fi; \
	# Locate the Ray head pod (resource/name form)
	HEAD_RES=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/node-type=head -o name | head -n1 2>/dev/null || true); \
	if [ -z "$$HEAD_RES" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Could not find Ray head pod in namespace $(NAMESPACE)$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 1; \
	fi; \
	# Start port-forward in background with nohup
	LOG_FILE=logs/portforward-dashboard-$(DASHBOARD_PORT).log; \
	nohup kubectl -n $(NAMESPACE) port-forward "$$HEAD_RES" $(DASHBOARD_PORT):$(DASHBOARD_PORT) --address 0.0.0.0 > "$$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 & \
	PF_PID=$$!; \
	echo "$$PF_PID" > "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	sleep 1; \
	if ps -p "$$PF_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward running (PID=$$PF_PID). Logs: $$LOG_FILE$(RESET)"; \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Access the dashboard at: http://127.0.0.1:$(DASHBOARD_PORT) or your host IP$(RESET)"; \
	else \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward failed to start. See $$LOG_FILE$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 1; \
	fi

.PHONY: port-forward-dashboard-stop
port-forward-dashboard-stop:
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	if [ ! -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] No PID file found (nothing to stop)$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 0; \
	fi; \
	PID=$$(cat "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" 2>/dev/null || true); \
	if [ -z "$$PID" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] PID file empty (nothing to stop)$(RESET)"; \
	  rm -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	  exit 0; \
	fi; \
	if ps -p "$$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Stopping port-forward (PID=$$PID)$(RESET)"; \
	  kill "$$PID" || true; \
	  sleep 1; \
	  if ps -p "$$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Force killing PID $$PID$(RESET)"; \
	    kill -9 "$$PID" || true; \
	  fi; \
	else \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] No running process for PID $$PID$(RESET)"; \
	fi; \
	rm -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward stopped$(RESET)"

.PHONY: _detect-node-ip
_detect-node-ip:
	@if [ -z "$(NODE_IP)" ]; then \
	  DETECTED_IP=$$(ip route get 1.1.1.1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($$i=="src") {print $$(i+1); exit}}'); \
	  if [ -z "$$DETECTED_IP" ]; then \
	    echo "$(RED)$(BOLD)Unable to auto-detect NODE_IP; please pass NODE_IP=...$(RESET)"; \
	    exit 1; \
	  fi; \
	  echo "Using auto-detected NODE_IP=$$DETECTED_IP"; \
	  echo "NODE_IP=$$DETECTED_IP" > .make.cached.env; \
	else \
	  echo "NODE_IP=$(NODE_IP)" > .make.cached.env; \
	fi

.PHONY: redeploy-clean
redeploy-clean: _ensure-tools
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Deleting RayService $(SERVICE_NAME)$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl delete rayservice $(SERVICE_NAME) -n $(NAMESPACE) --ignore-not-found=true || true; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Waiting briefly for pods to terminate$(RESET)"; \
	sleep 3; \
	PODS=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes -o name 2>/dev/null || true); \
		if [ -n "$$PODS" ]; then \
			printf "%b\n" "Found lingering Ray pods, forcing deletion:"; printf "%b\n" "$$PODS"; \
	  kubectl delete $$PODS -n $(NAMESPACE) --force --grace-period=0 || true; \
	fi; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Verifying no Ray pods remain$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes || true; \
	if command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Checking GPU processes$(RESET)"; \
	  nvidia-smi || true; \
	fi

.PHONY: deploy-apply
deploy-apply: _ensure-tools
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Applying $(RAYSERVICE_FILE)$(RESET)"; \
		kubectl apply -n $(NAMESPACE) -f $(RAYSERVICE_FILE); \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Waiting for Ray pods to appear$(RESET)"; \
	for i in $$(seq 1 60); do \
	  CNT=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes -o name 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '); \
			if [ "$$CNT" -gt 0 ]; then printf "%b\n" "Found $$CNT Ray pods"; break; fi; \
	  sleep 2; \
	done; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Waiting for Ray pods Ready (timeout 10m)$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl wait --for=condition=ready pod -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes --timeout=600s; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Waiting for Serve endpoints to be ready$(RESET)"; \
	for i in $$(seq 1 150); do \
	  EP=$$(kubectl get endpoints $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[*].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
			if [ -n "$$EP" ]; then printf "%b\n" "Serve endpoints: $$EP"; break; fi; \
	  sleep 2; \
	done; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Ray pods Ready$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -o wide | sed -n '1,200p'

.PHONY: smoke-health
smoke-health: _ensure-tools _detect-node-ip
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		. ./.make.cached.env; \
		IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
		ENDPOINT_IP=http://$${NODE_IP}:$(NODE_PORT); \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Checking health via Ingress: $$ENDPOINT_IP/health (Host: $$HOST)$(RESET)"; \
		RESOLVE=$$(getent hosts $$HOST 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $$1}' | head -n1 || true); \
		if [ -n "$$RESOLVE" ] && [ "$$RESOLVE" != "$$NODE_IP" ]; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Warning: $$HOST resolves to $$RESOLVE, expected $$NODE_IP$(RESET)"; \
		fi; \
		CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
		RES=$$(curl -s -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
		printf "%b\n" "Health code: $$CODE body: $$RES"; \
		if [ "$$CODE" != "200" ] || ! echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Ingress not healthy (code=$$CODE), trying direct pod endpoint fallback$(RESET)"; \
			POD_IP=$$(kubectl get endpoints embedding-service-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
			if [ -n "$$POD_IP" ]; then \
				printf "%b\n" "Trying http://$$POD_IP:8000/health"; \
				CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://$$POD_IP:8000/health || true); \
				RES=$$(curl -s http://$$POD_IP:8000/health || true); \
				printf "%b\n" "Fallback code: $$CODE body: $$RES"; \
				if [ "$$CODE" != "200" ] || ! echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then \
					printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Fallback health also not healthy$(RESET)"; \
					exit 1; \
				fi; \
			else \
				printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Could not determine pod IP for fallback$(RESET)"; \
				exit 1; \
			fi; \
		fi; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Health OK$(RESET)"

.PHONY: quick-load-test
quick-load-test: _ensure-tools _detect-node-ip
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		. ./.make.cached.env; \
		IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
	TARGET_URL=http://$$HOST:$(NODE_PORT); \
	HEALTH_URL=http://$${NODE_IP}:$(NODE_PORT); \
	printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Debug: HOST=$$HOST TARGET_URL=$$TARGET_URL HEALTH_URL=$$HEALTH_URL$(RESET)"; \
	# Prefer ingress: health wait (skip if SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT=true)
	if [ "$${SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT:-false}" != "true" ]; then \
	  START=$$(date +%s); \
	  OK=false; \
	  while :; do \
	    CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$HEALTH_URL/health || true); \
	    RES=$$(curl -s -H "Host: $$HOST" $$HEALTH_URL/health || true); \
	    if [ "$$CODE" = "200" ] && echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then OK=true; break; fi; \
	    NOW=$$(date +%s); \
	    ELAPSED=$$((NOW-START)); \
	    if [ "$$ELAPSED" -ge "$(INGRESS_WAIT_SECS)" ]; then break; fi; \
	    sleep 2; \
	  done; \
	  if [ "$$OK" != "true" ]; then \
	    if [ "$(USE_INGRESS_ONLY)" = "true" ]; then \
	      printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Ingress not healthy after $(INGRESS_WAIT_SECS)s (last code=$$CODE). Aborting per USE_INGRESS_ONLY=true$(RESET)"; \
	      exit 1; \
	    else \
	      POD_IP=$$(kubectl get endpoints $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
	      if [ -n "$$POD_IP" ]; then \
	        TARGET_URL=http://$$POD_IP:8000; \
	        printf "%b\n" "Ingress not ready (last code=$$CODE), falling back to direct pod URL: $$TARGET_URL"; \
	      fi; \
	    fi; \
	  fi; \
	fi; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Running load test to $$TARGET_URL: R=$(TEST_REQUESTS) C=$(TEST_CONCURRENCY) segmentation=$(TEST_SEGMENTATION)$(RESET)"; \
	python3 working_dir/load_test.py --url $$TARGET_URL --requests $(TEST_REQUESTS) --concurrency $(TEST_CONCURRENCY) --segmentation $(TEST_SEGMENTATION)

.PHONY: quick-load-test-ingress
quick-load-test-ingress: smoke-health
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	. ./.make.cached.env; \
	IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
	URL=http://$$HOST:$(NODE_PORT); \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test-ingress] Running ingress-only load test: $$URL R=$(TEST_REQUESTS) C=$(TEST_CONCURRENCY) segmentation=$(TEST_SEGMENTATION)$(RESET)"; \
	python3 working_dir/load_test.py --url $$URL --requests $(TEST_REQUESTS) --concurrency $(TEST_CONCURRENCY) --segmentation $(TEST_SEGMENTATION)

.PHONY: redeploy
redeploy: redeploy-clean deploy-apply smoke-health
	@printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[redeploy] Completed cleanup, deploy, and health verification$(RESET)"

.PHONY: redeploy-and-test
redeploy-and-test: redeploy quick-load-test
	@printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[redeploy-and-test] Completed end-to-end redeploy with load test$(RESET)"

response.value:
**Investigating HEAD_RES issues**

I'm looking into why the `HEAD_RES` variable is showing as empty. It might be related to context or quoting problems. In the Makefile, we have this command with `set -euo pipefail`, and I thought the check for emptiness using `if [ -z "$HEAD_RES" ]; then` would catch that. But the logs show the emptiness only later, making me wonder if there are hidden characters like spaces or carriage returns in `HEAD_RES`. It's puzzling since we seem to be setting it properly, yet it isn't recognized correctly.

**Examining nohup and variable persistence**

I’m trying to understand the persistence of variables in a single `sh -c` shell, particularly regarding the `nohup` command. While I thought it might start a subshell, it doesn’t seem to. Instead, I could run command substitution inline with `nohup`, which means I wouldn't need to set `HEAD_RES`. 

However, before proceeding, I want to ensure we check for emptiness first. I'm considering moving the resource command to an earlier point, but I've noticed it might behave inconsistently. Let's find a clean way to handle this.

**Improving command error handling**

I’m considering that line continuation might be interfering when using `head -n1 2>/dev/null || true`. The `||` appears to apply to the pipeline, but I think I should simplify this process. I’ll remove `|| true` and let `set -e` handle errors, although I still want to manage failures gracefully. 

To improve reliability, I’ll modify the Makefile to compute `RES` on the same line and echo out the result. Plus, I should include a check for `command -v kubectl`. Let’s implement these changes and add debug prints.

PYTHON_VERSION = 3.12.1 # keep minor versions syncd

RED := \033[0;31m
GREEN := \033[0;32m
YELLOW := \033[0;33m

	@if [ -z $(PYTHON_VERSION) ]; then \
		echo "$(RED)$(BOLD)This is the python verion $(PYTHON_VERSION)$(RESET)"; \
		exit 1; \

	@echo "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)Creating a virtual environment$(RESET)"

		echo "Python version $(PYTHON_VERSION) is not installed."; \
		echo "Installing this version of Python..."; \
		pyenv install -s $(PYTHON_VERSION); \
	fi

		pyenv virtualenv $(PYTHON_VERSION) $(VIRTUALENV_NAME); else \

	@pre-commit install

	  printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Could not find Ray head pod in namespace $(NAMESPACE)$(RESET)"; \

	fi; \
	# Start port-forward in background with nohup
	LOG_FILE=logs/portforward-dashboard-$(DASHBOARD_PORT).log; \
	nohup kubectl -n $(NAMESPACE) port-forward "$$HEAD_RES" $(DASHBOARD_PORT):$(DASHBOARD_PORT) --address 0.0.0.0 > "$$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 & \
	PF_PID=$$!; \
	echo "$$PF_PID" > "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	sleep 1; \
	if ps -p "$$PF_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward running (PID=$$PF_PID). Logs: $$LOG_FILE$(RESET)"; \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Access the dashboard at: http://127.0.0.1:$(DASHBOARD_PORT) or your host IP$(RESET)"; \
	else \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward failed to start. See $$LOG_FILE$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 1; \
	fi

.PHONY: port-forward-dashboard-stop
port-forward-dashboard-stop:
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	if [ ! -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] No PID file found (nothing to stop)$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 0; \
	fi; \
	PID=$$(cat "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" 2>/dev/null || true); \
	if [ -z "$$PID" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] PID file empty (nothing to stop)$(RESET)"; \
	  rm -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	  exit 0; \
	fi; \
	if ps -p "$$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Stopping port-forward (PID=$$PID)$(RESET)"; \
	  kill "$$PID" || true; \
	  sleep 1; \
	  if ps -p "$$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Force killing PID $$PID$(RESET)"; \
	    kill -9 "$$PID" || true; \
	  fi; \
	else \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] No running process for PID $$PID$(RESET)"; \
	fi; \
	rm -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward stopped$(RESET)"

.PHONY: _detect-node-ip
_detect-node-ip:
	@if [ -z "$(NODE_IP)" ]; then \
	  DETECTED_IP=$$(ip route get 1.1.1.1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($$i=="src") {print $$(i+1); exit}}'); \
	  if [ -z "$$DETECTED_IP" ]; then \
	    echo "$(RED)$(BOLD)Unable to auto-detect NODE_IP; please pass NODE_IP=...$(RESET)"; \
	    exit 1; \
	  fi; \
	  echo "Using auto-detected NODE_IP=$$DETECTED_IP"; \
	  echo "NODE_IP=$$DETECTED_IP" > .make.cached.env; \
	else \
	  echo "NODE_IP=$(NODE_IP)" > .make.cached.env; \
	fi

.PHONY: redeploy-clean
redeploy-clean: _ensure-tools
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Deleting RayService $(SERVICE_NAME)$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl delete rayservice $(SERVICE_NAME) -n $(NAMESPACE) --ignore-not-found=true || true; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Waiting briefly for pods to terminate$(RESET)"; \
	sleep 3; \
	PODS=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes -o name 2>/dev/null || true); \
		if [ -n "$$PODS" ]; then \
			printf "%b\n" "Found lingering Ray pods, forcing deletion:"; printf "%b\n" "$$PODS"; \
	  kubectl delete $$PODS -n $(NAMESPACE) --force --grace-period=0 || true; \
	fi; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Verifying no Ray pods remain$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes || true; \
	if command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Checking GPU processes$(RESET)"; \
	  nvidia-smi || true; \
	fi

.PHONY: deploy-apply
deploy-apply: _ensure-tools
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Applying $(RAYSERVICE_FILE)$(RESET)"; \
		kubectl apply -n $(NAMESPACE) -f $(RAYSERVICE_FILE); \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Waiting for Ray pods to appear$(RESET)"; \
	for i in $$(seq 1 60); do \
	  CNT=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes -o name 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '); \
			if [ "$$CNT" -gt 0 ]; then printf "%b\n" "Found $$CNT Ray pods"; break; fi; \
	  sleep 2; \
	done; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Waiting for Ray pods Ready (timeout 10m)$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl wait --for=condition=ready pod -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes --timeout=600s; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Waiting for Serve endpoints to be ready$(RESET)"; \
	for i in $$(seq 1 150); do \
	  EP=$$(kubectl get endpoints $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[*].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
			if [ -n "$$EP" ]; then printf "%b\n" "Serve endpoints: $$EP"; break; fi; \
	  sleep 2; \
	done; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Ray pods Ready$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -o wide | sed -n '1,200p'

.PHONY: smoke-health
smoke-health: _ensure-tools _detect-node-ip
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		. ./.make.cached.env; \
		IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
		ENDPOINT_IP=http://$${NODE_IP}:$(NODE_PORT); \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Checking health via Ingress: $$ENDPOINT_IP/health (Host: $$HOST)$(RESET)"; \
		RESOLVE=$$(getent hosts $$HOST 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $$1}' | head -n1 || true); \
		if [ -n "$$RESOLVE" ] && [ "$$RESOLVE" != "$$NODE_IP" ]; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Warning: $$HOST resolves to $$RESOLVE, expected $$NODE_IP$(RESET)"; \
		fi; \
		CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
		RES=$$(curl -s -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
		printf "%b\n" "Health code: $$CODE body: $$RES"; \
		if [ "$$CODE" != "200" ] || ! echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Ingress not healthy (code=$$CODE), trying direct pod endpoint fallback$(RESET)"; \
			POD_IP=$$(kubectl get endpoints embedding-service-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
			if [ -n "$$POD_IP" ]; then \
				printf "%b\n" "Trying http://$$POD_IP:8000/health"; \
				CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://$$POD_IP:8000/health || true); \
				RES=$$(curl -s http://$$POD_IP:8000/health || true); \
				printf "%b\n" "Fallback code: $$CODE body: $$RES"; \
				if [ "$$CODE" != "200" ] || ! echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then \
					printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Fallback health also not healthy$(RESET)"; \
					exit 1; \
				fi; \
			else \
				printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Could not determine pod IP for fallback$(RESET)"; \
				exit 1; \
			fi; \
		fi; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Health OK$(RESET)"

.PHONY: quick-load-test
quick-load-test: _ensure-tools _detect-node-ip
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		. ./.make.cached.env; \
		IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
	TARGET_URL=http://$$HOST:$(NODE_PORT); \
	HEALTH_URL=http://$${NODE_IP}:$(NODE_PORT); \
	printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Debug: HOST=$$HOST TARGET_URL=$$TARGET_URL HEALTH_URL=$$HEALTH_URL$(RESET)"; \
	# Prefer ingress: health wait (skip if SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT=true)
	if [ "$${SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT:-false}" != "true" ]; then \
	  START=$$(date +%s); \
	  OK=false; \
	  while :; do \
	    CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$HEALTH_URL/health || true); \
	    RES=$$(curl -s -H "Host: $$HOST" $$HEALTH_URL/health || true); \
	    if [ "$$CODE" = "200" ] && echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then OK=true; break; fi; \
	    NOW=$$(date +%s); \
	    ELAPSED=$$((NOW-START)); \
	    if [ "$$ELAPSED" -ge "$(INGRESS_WAIT_SECS)" ]; then break; fi; \
	    sleep 2; \
	  done; \
	  if [ "$$OK" != "true" ]; then \
	    if [ "$(USE_INGRESS_ONLY)" = "true" ]; then \
	      printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Ingress not healthy after $(INGRESS_WAIT_SECS)s (last code=$$CODE). Aborting per USE_INGRESS_ONLY=true$(RESET)"; \
	      exit 1; \
	    else \
	      POD_IP=$$(kubectl get endpoints $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
	      if [ -n "$$POD_IP" ]; then \
	        TARGET_URL=http://$$POD_IP:8000; \
	        printf "%b\n" "Ingress not ready (last code=$$CODE), falling back to direct pod URL: $$TARGET_URL"; \
	      fi; \
	    fi; \
	  fi; \
	fi; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Running load test to $$TARGET_URL: R=$(TEST_REQUESTS) C=$(TEST_CONCURRENCY) segmentation=$(TEST_SEGMENTATION)$(RESET)"; \
	python3 working_dir/load_test.py --url $$TARGET_URL --requests $(TEST_REQUESTS) --concurrency $(TEST_CONCURRENCY) --segmentation $(TEST_SEGMENTATION)

.PHONY: quick-load-test-ingress
quick-load-test-ingress: smoke-health
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	. ./.make.cached.env; \
	IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
	URL=http://$$HOST:$(NODE_PORT); \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test-ingress] Running ingress-only load test: $$URL R=$(TEST_REQUESTS) C=$(TEST_CONCURRENCY) segmentation=$(TEST_SEGMENTATION)$(RESET)"; \
	python3 working_dir/load_test.py --url $$URL --requests $(TEST_REQUESTS) --concurrency $(TEST_CONCURRENCY) --segmentation $(TEST_SEGMENTATION)

.PHONY: redeploy
redeploy: redeploy-clean deploy-apply smoke-health
	@printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[redeploy] Completed cleanup, deploy, and health verification$(RESET)"

.PHONY: redeploy-and-test
redeploy-and-test: redeploy quick-load-test
	@printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[redeploy-and-test] Completed end-to-end redeploy with load test$(RESET)"

**Investigating variable issues**

I’m looking into the variable HEAD_RES and its export issues across logical lines. It seems that a line break without a trailing backslash could cause it not to export properly. The error message about an empty resource name indicates that "$HEAD_RES" might be empty because of a broken backslash continuation, possibly due to a blank line. In our Makefile, I noticed there’s a comment line which could break the chain. I’ll inspect that snippet closely!

**Clarifying variable transfer in shell**

This explains why HEAD_RES isn't available in the new shell on the next line. The comment line begins with a tab and a '#', but it’s treated as a shell comment. Since it's its own line without a trailing backslash, Make spawns a new shell for that line, which only executes the comment (a no-op), causing HEAD_RES not to carry over. To preserve variables, we should keep everything in the same shell, which could involve using backslash continuation or simply removing the separate comment line.

**Ensuring backslash continuity**

I need to make sure that backslash continuation is maintained throughout. One option is placing the comment after a backslash, like "fi; \\\n\t# Start ...", but it’s still a separate line. The trick is to continue with a colon for a no-op and backslash, or better yet, just remove the comment line entirely. It’s easier that way to keep the same shell context. So, I'll focus on removing that isolated comment line to simplify things!

**Modifying the comment**

I think it’s a good idea to remove the comment "# Start port-forward in background with nohup" altogether or perhaps merge it into the previous echo command. That way, I can streamline the script and keep things clean. After making this change, I’ll definitely want to test it again to make sure everything works as expected. Simplifying the code should help avoid confusion and ensure variable continuity!

RED := \033[0;31m
GREEN := \033[0;32m
YELLOW := \033[0;33m

.PHONY: _python_version

	@if [ -z $(PYTHON_VERSION) ]; then \
		echo "$(RED)$(BOLD)This is the python verion $(PYTHON_VERSION)$(RESET)"; \
		exit 1; \
	fi


.PHONY: pyenv
pyenv: | _python_version # create a python virtual env

		echo "Python version $(PYTHON_VERSION) is not installed."; \

DASHBOARD_PID_FILE ?= run/dashboard_pf.pid

.PHONY: port-forward-dashboard

	@set -euo pipefail; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Starting port-forward to Ray Dashboard on port $(DASHBOARD_PORT)$(RESET)"; \
	# Ensure run/ and logs/ directories exist

	# Check if a previous port-forward is running
	if [ -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" ]; then \

	  if [ -n "$$OLD_PID" ] && ps -p "$$OLD_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Existing port-forward detected (PID=$$OLD_PID). Leaving it running.$(RESET)"; \

	if ps -p "$$PF_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward running (PID=$$PF_PID). Logs: $$LOG_FILE$(RESET)"; \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Access the dashboard at: http://127.0.0.1:$(DASHBOARD_PORT) or your host IP$(RESET)"; \
	else \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward failed to start. See $$LOG_FILE$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 1; \
	fi

.PHONY: port-forward-dashboard-stop
port-forward-dashboard-stop:
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	if [ ! -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] No PID file found (nothing to stop)$(RESET)"; \

	PID=$$(cat "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" 2>/dev/null || true); \

	else \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] No running process for PID $$PID$(RESET)"; \
	fi; \
	rm -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward stopped$(RESET)"

	@if [ -z "$(NODE_IP)" ]; then \

	  echo "Using auto-detected NODE_IP=$$DETECTED_IP"; \
	  echo "NODE_IP=$$DETECTED_IP" > .make.cached.env; \

	fi

.PHONY: redeploy-clean
redeploy-clean: _ensure-tools
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Deleting RayService $(SERVICE_NAME)$(RESET)"; \

	sleep 3; \

	  kubectl delete $$PODS -n $(NAMESPACE) --force --grace-period=0 || true; \
	fi; \

	for i in $$(seq 1 60); do \

	  sleep 2; \
	done; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Waiting for Ray pods Ready (timeout 10m)$(RESET)"; \

	  EP=$$(kubectl get endpoints $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[*].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
			if [ -n "$$EP" ]; then printf "%b\n" "Serve endpoints: $$EP"; break; fi; \

.PHONY: smoke-health
smoke-health: _ensure-tools _detect-node-ip
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		. ./.make.cached.env; \
		IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
		ENDPOINT_IP=http://$${NODE_IP}:$(NODE_PORT); \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Checking health via Ingress: $$ENDPOINT_IP/health (Host: $$HOST)$(RESET)"; \
		RESOLVE=$$(getent hosts $$HOST 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $$1}' | head -n1 || true); \
		if [ -n "$$RESOLVE" ] && [ "$$RESOLVE" != "$$NODE_IP" ]; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Warning: $$HOST resolves to $$RESOLVE, expected $$NODE_IP$(RESET)"; \
		fi; \
		CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
		RES=$$(curl -s -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
		printf "%b\n" "Health code: $$CODE body: $$RES"; \
		if [ "$$CODE" != "200" ] || ! echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Ingress not healthy (code=$$CODE), trying direct pod endpoint fallback$(RESET)"; \
			POD_IP=$$(kubectl get endpoints embedding-service-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
			if [ -n "$$POD_IP" ]; then \
				printf "%b\n" "Trying http://$$POD_IP:8000/health"; \
				CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://$$POD_IP:8000/health || true); \
				RES=$$(curl -s http://$$POD_IP:8000/health || true); \
				printf "%b\n" "Fallback code: $$CODE body: $$RES"; \
				if [ "$$CODE" != "200" ] || ! echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then \
					printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Fallback health also not healthy$(RESET)"; \
					exit 1; \
				fi; \
			else \
				printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Could not determine pod IP for fallback$(RESET)"; \
				exit 1; \
			fi; \
		fi; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Health OK$(RESET)"

.PHONY: quick-load-test
quick-load-test: _ensure-tools _detect-node-ip
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		. ./.make.cached.env; \
		IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
	TARGET_URL=http://$$HOST:$(NODE_PORT); \
	HEALTH_URL=http://$${NODE_IP}:$(NODE_PORT); \
	printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Debug: HOST=$$HOST TARGET_URL=$$TARGET_URL HEALTH_URL=$$HEALTH_URL$(RESET)"; \
	# Prefer ingress: health wait (skip if SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT=true)
	if [ "$${SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT:-false}" != "true" ]; then \
	  START=$$(date +%s); \
	  OK=false; \
	  while :; do \
	    CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$HEALTH_URL/health || true); \
	    RES=$$(curl -s -H "Host: $$HOST" $$HEALTH_URL/health || true); \
	    if [ "$$CODE" = "200" ] && echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then OK=true; break; fi; \
	    NOW=$$(date +%s); \
	    ELAPSED=$$((NOW-START)); \
	    if [ "$$ELAPSED" -ge "$(INGRESS_WAIT_SECS)" ]; then break; fi; \
	    sleep 2; \
	  done; \
	  if [ "$$OK" != "true" ]; then \
	    if [ "$(USE_INGRESS_ONLY)" = "true" ]; then \
	      printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Ingress not healthy after $(INGRESS_WAIT_SECS)s (last code=$$CODE). Aborting per USE_INGRESS_ONLY=true$(RESET)"; \
	      exit 1; \
	    else \
	      POD_IP=$$(kubectl get endpoints $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
	      if [ -n "$$POD_IP" ]; then \
	        TARGET_URL=http://$$POD_IP:8000; \
	        printf "%b\n" "Ingress not ready (last code=$$CODE), falling back to direct pod URL: $$TARGET_URL"; \
	      fi; \
	    fi; \
	  fi; \
	fi; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Running load test to $$TARGET_URL: R=$(TEST_REQUESTS) C=$(TEST_CONCURRENCY) segmentation=$(TEST_SEGMENTATION)$(RESET)"; \
	python3 working_dir/load_test.py --url $$TARGET_URL --requests $(TEST_REQUESTS) --concurrency $(TEST_CONCURRENCY) --segmentation $(TEST_SEGMENTATION)

.PHONY: quick-load-test-ingress
quick-load-test-ingress: smoke-health
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	. ./.make.cached.env; \
	IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
	URL=http://$$HOST:$(NODE_PORT); \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test-ingress] Running ingress-only load test: $$URL R=$(TEST_REQUESTS) C=$(TEST_CONCURRENCY) segmentation=$(TEST_SEGMENTATION)$(RESET)"; \
	python3 working_dir/load_test.py --url $$URL --requests $(TEST_REQUESTS) --concurrency $(TEST_CONCURRENCY) --segmentation $(TEST_SEGMENTATION)

.PHONY: redeploy
redeploy: redeploy-clean deploy-apply smoke-health
	@printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[redeploy] Completed cleanup, deploy, and health verification$(RESET)"

.PHONY: redeploy-and-test
redeploy-and-test: redeploy quick-load-test
	@printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[redeploy-and-test] Completed end-to-end redeploy with load test$(RESET)"

VIRTUALENV_NAME := $(shell basename $(CURDIR))

		pyenv install -s $(PYTHON_VERSION); \

		pyenv virtualenv $(PYTHON_VERSION) $(VIRTUALENV_NAME); else \

	@pip install --upgrade pip

.PHONY: port-forward-dashboard
 .SILENT: port-forward-dashboard
port-forward-dashboard: _ensure-tools
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Starting port-forward to Ray Dashboard on port $(DASHBOARD_PORT)$(RESET)"; \
	mkdir -p run logs; \
	if [ -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" ]; then \
