# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Kubernetes/RayService deploy + test helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Ray/K8s variables (override at invocation if needed)
SERVICE_NAME ?= embedding-service
RAYSERVICE_FILE ?= k8s/rayservice-local.yaml
NAMESPACE ?= default

# Ingress testing vars
# If NODE_IP is not provided, we'll try to detect it at runtime
NODE_PORT ?= 30333
TEST_REQUESTS ?= 200
TEST_CONCURRENCY ?= 10
TEST_SEGMENTATION ?= false
USE_INGRESS_ONLY ?= true
INGRESS_WAIT_SECS ?= 60
INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS ?= 90

.PHONY: _ensure-tools
_ensure-tools:
	@command -v kubectl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "kubectl not found in PATH"; exit 1; }
	@command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "curl not found in PATH"; exit 1; }
	@command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "python3 not found in PATH"; exit 1; }

# Ray dashboard port-forward settings
DASHBOARD_PORT ?= 8265
DASHBOARD_PID_FILE ?= run/dashboard_pf.pid

.PHONY: port-forward-dashboard
.SILENT: port-forward-dashboard
port-forward-dashboard: _ensure-tools
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Starting port-forward to Ray Dashboard on port $(DASHBOARD_PORT)$(RESET)"; \
	mkdir -p run logs; \
	if [ -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" ]; then \
	  OLD_PID=$$(cat "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" 2>/dev/null || true); \
	  if [ -n "$$OLD_PID" ] && ps -p "$$OLD_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Existing port-forward detected (PID=$$OLD_PID). Leaving it running.$(RESET)"; \
	    exit 0; \
	  fi; \
	fi; \
	HEAD_RES=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/node-type=head -o name | head -n1); \
	printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Using resource: $$HEAD_RES$(RESET)"; \
	if [ -z "$$HEAD_RES" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Could not find Ray head pod in namespace $(NAMESPACE)$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 1; \
	fi; \
	LOG_FILE=logs/portforward-dashboard-$(DASHBOARD_PORT).log; \
	nohup kubectl -n $(NAMESPACE) port-forward "$$HEAD_RES" $(DASHBOARD_PORT):$(DASHBOARD_PORT) --address 0.0.0.0 > "$$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 & \
	PF_PID=$$!; \
	echo "$$PF_PID" > "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	sleep 1; \
	if ps -p "$$PF_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward running (PID=$$PF_PID). Logs: $$LOG_FILE$(RESET)"; \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Access the dashboard at: http://127.0.0.1:$(DASHBOARD_PORT) or your host IP$(RESET)"; \
	else \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward failed to start. See $$LOG_FILE$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 1; \
	fi

.PHONY: port-forward-dashboard-stop
.SILENT: port-forward-dashboard-stop
port-forward-dashboard-stop:
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	if [ ! -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] No PID file found (nothing to stop)$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 0; \
	fi; \
	PID=$$(cat "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" 2>/dev/null || true); \
	if [ -z "$$PID" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] PID file empty (nothing to stop)$(RESET)"; \
	  rm -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	  exit 0; \
	fi; \
	if ps -p "$$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Stopping port-forward (PID=$$PID)$(RESET)"; \
	  kill "$$PID" || true; \
	  sleep 1; \
	  if ps -p "$$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Force killing PID $$PID$(RESET)"; \
	    kill -9 "$$PID" || true; \
	  fi; \
	else \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] No running process for PID $$PID$(RESET)"; \
	fi; \
	rm -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward stopped$(RESET)"

.PHONY: _detect-node-ip
_detect-node-ip:
	@if [ -z "$(NODE_IP)" ]; then \
	  DETECTED_IP=$$(ip route get 1.1.1.1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($$i=="src") {print $$(i+1); exit}}'); \
	  if [ -z "$$DETECTED_IP" ]; then \
	    echo "$(RED)$(BOLD)Unable to auto-detect NODE_IP; please pass NODE_IP=...$(RESET)"; \
	    exit 1; \
	  fi; \
	  echo "Using auto-detected NODE_IP=$$DETECTED_IP"; \
	  echo "NODE_IP=$$DETECTED_IP" > .make.cached.env; \
	else \
	  echo "NODE_IP=$(NODE_IP)" > .make.cached.env; \
	fi

.PHONY: redeploy-clean
redeploy-clean: _ensure-tools
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Deleting RayService $(SERVICE_NAME)$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl delete rayservice $(SERVICE_NAME) -n $(NAMESPACE) --ignore-not-found=true || true; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Waiting briefly for pods to terminate$(RESET)"; \
	sleep 3; \
	PODS=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes -o name 2>/dev/null || true); \
		if [ -n "$$PODS" ]; then \
			printf "%b\n" "Found lingering Ray pods, forcing deletion:"; printf "%b\n" "$$PODS"; \
	  kubectl delete $$PODS -n $(NAMESPACE) --force --grace-period=0 || true; \
	fi; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Verifying no Ray pods remain$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes || true; \
	if command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Checking GPU processes$(RESET)"; \
	  nvidia-smi || true; \
	fi

.PHONY: deploy-apply
deploy-apply: _ensure-tools
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Applying $(RAYSERVICE_FILE)$(RESET)"; \
		kubectl apply -n $(NAMESPACE) -f $(RAYSERVICE_FILE); \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Waiting for Ray pods to appear$(RESET)"; \
	for i in $$(seq 1 60); do \
	  CNT=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes -o name 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '); \
			if [ "$$CNT" -gt 0 ]; then printf "%b\n" "Found $$CNT Ray pods"; break; fi; \
	  sleep 2; \
	done; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Waiting for Ray pods Ready (timeout 10m)$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl wait --for=condition=ready pod -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes --timeout=600s; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Waiting for Serve endpoints to be ready$(RESET)"; \
	for i in $$(seq 1 150); do \
	  EP=$$(kubectl get endpoints $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[*].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
			if [ -n "$$EP" ]; then printf "%b\n" "Serve endpoints: $$EP"; break; fi; \
	  sleep 2; \
	done; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Ray pods Ready$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -o wide | sed -n '1,200p'

.PHONY: smoke-health
smoke-health: _ensure-tools _detect-node-ip
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		. ./.make.cached.env; \
		IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
		ENDPOINT_IP=http://$${NODE_IP}:$(NODE_PORT); \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Checking health via Ingress: $$ENDPOINT_IP/health (Host: $$HOST)$(RESET)"; \
		RESOLVE=$$(getent hosts $$HOST 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $$1}' | head -n1 || true); \
		if [ -n "$$RESOLVE" ] && [ "$$RESOLVE" != "$$NODE_IP" ]; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Warning: $$HOST resolves to $$RESOLVE, expected $$NODE_IP$(RESET)"; \
		fi; \
		CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
		RES=$$(curl -s -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
		printf "%b\n" "Health code: $$CODE body: $$RES"; \
		if [ "$$CODE" != "200" ] || ! echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Ingress not healthy (code=$$CODE), trying direct pod endpoint fallback$(RESET)"; \
			POD_IP=$$(kubectl get endpoints embedding-service-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
			if [ -n "$$POD_IP" ]; then \
				printf "%b\n" "Trying http://$$POD_IP:8000/health"; \
				CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://$$POD_IP:8000/health || true); \
				RES=$$(curl -s http://$$POD_IP:8000/health || true); \
				printf "%b\n" "Fallback code: $$CODE body: $$RES"; \
				if [ "$$CODE" != "200" ] || ! echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then \
					printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Fallback health also not healthy$(RESET)"; \
					exit 1; \
				fi; \
				printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Fallback OK; waiting up to $(INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS)s for Ingress to become healthy$(RESET)"; \
				START=$$(date +%s); OK=false; \
				while :; do \
				  CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
				  RES=$$(curl -s -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
				  if [ "$$CODE" = "200" ] && echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then OK=true; break; fi; \
				  NOW=$$(date +%s); ELAPSED=$$((NOW-START)); \
				  if [ "$$ELAPSED" -ge "$(INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS)" ]; then break; fi; \
				  sleep 2; \
				done; \
				if [ "$$OK" != "true" ]; then \
				  printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Ingress still not healthy after $(INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS)s (last code=$$CODE). Aborting.$(RESET)"; \
				  exit 1; \
				fi; \
			else \
				printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Could not determine pod IP for fallback$(RESET)"; \
				exit 1; \
			fi; \
		fi; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Health OK$(RESET)"

.PHONY: serve-status
.SILENT: serve-status
serve-status:
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	HEAD_POD=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/node-type=head -o name | head -n1 | cut -d/ -f2); \
	if [ -z "$$HEAD_POD" ]; then echo "No Ray head pod found"; exit 1; fi; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[serve-status] Querying Serve status from $$HEAD_POD$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl exec -i -n $(NAMESPACE) $$HEAD_POD -- python3 - <<-'PY'
	from ray import serve
	try:
	    status = serve.status()
	    try:
	        d = status.to_dict()
	    except Exception:
	        import dataclasses, json
	        d = dataclasses.asdict(status)
	    import json
	    print(json.dumps(d, indent=2))
	except Exception as e:
	    print(f"error: {e}")
	PY

.PHONY: quick-load-test
quick-load-test: _ensure-tools _detect-node-ip
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		. ./.make.cached.env; \
		IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
	TARGET_URL=http://$$HOST:$(NODE_PORT); \
	HEALTH_URL=http://$${NODE_IP}:$(NODE_PORT); \
	printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Debug: HOST=$$HOST TARGET_URL=$$TARGET_URL HEALTH_URL=$$HEALTH_URL$(RESET)"; \
	# Prefer ingress: health wait (skip if SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT=true)
	if [ "$${SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT:-false}" != "true" ]; then \
	  START=$$(date +%s); \
	  OK=false; \
	  while :; do \
	    CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$HEALTH_URL/health || true); \
	    RES=$$(curl -s -H "Host: $$HOST" $$HEALTH_URL/health || true); \
	    if [ "$$CODE" = "200" ] && echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then OK=true; break; fi; \
	    NOW=$$(date +%s); \
	    ELAPSED=$$((NOW-START)); \
	    if [ "$$ELAPSED" -ge "$(INGRESS_WAIT_SECS)" ]; then break; fi; \
	    sleep 2; \
	  done; \
	  if [ "$$OK" != "true" ]; then \
	    if [ "$(USE_INGRESS_ONLY)" = "true" ]; then \
	      printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Ingress not healthy after $(INGRESS_WAIT_SECS)s (last code=$$CODE). Aborting per USE_INGRESS_ONLY=true$(RESET)"; \
	      exit 1; \
	    else \
	      POD_IP=$$(kubectl get endpoints $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
	      if [ -n "$$POD_IP" ]; then \
	        TARGET_URL=http://$$POD_IP:8000; \
	        printf "%b\n" "Ingress not ready (last code=$$CODE), falling back to direct pod URL: $$TARGET_URL"; \
	      fi; \
	    fi; \
	  fi; \
	fi; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Running load test to $$TARGET_URL: R=$(TEST_REQUESTS) C=$(TEST_CONCURRENCY) segmentation=$(TEST_SEGMENTATION)$(RESET)"; \
	python3 working_dir/load_test.py --url $$TARGET_URL --requests $(TEST_REQUESTS) --concurrency $(TEST_CONCURRENCY) --segmentation $(TEST_SEGMENTATION)

.PHONY: quick-load-test-ingress

.PHONY: _python_version

.PHONY: pyenv

		echo "Python version $(PYTHON_VERSION) is not installed."; \
		echo "Installing this version of Python..."; \
		pyenv install -s $(PYTHON_VERSION); \
	fi
	@if ! pyenv versions --bare | grep -q $(VIRTUALENV_NAME); then \
		pyenv virtualenv $(PYTHON_VERSION) $(VIRTUALENV_NAME); else \
		echo "Virtual environment $(VIRTUALENV_NAME) already exists."; \
	fi
	@pyenv local $(VIRTUALENV_NAME)
	@pip install --upgrade pip

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Kubernetes/RayService deploy + test helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Ray/K8s variables (override at invocation if needed)
SERVICE_NAME ?= embedding-service
RAYSERVICE_FILE ?= k8s/rayservice-local.yaml
NAMESPACE ?= default

# Ingress testing vars
# If NODE_IP is not provided, we'll try to detect it at runtime
NODE_PORT ?= 30333
TEST_REQUESTS ?= 200
TEST_CONCURRENCY ?= 10
TEST_SEGMENTATION ?= false
USE_INGRESS_ONLY ?= true
INGRESS_WAIT_SECS ?= 60
INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS ?= 90

.PHONY: _ensure-tools
_ensure-tools:
	@command -v kubectl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "kubectl not found in PATH"; exit 1; }
	@command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "curl not found in PATH"; exit 1; }
	@command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "python3 not found in PATH"; exit 1; }

# Ray dashboard port-forward settings
DASHBOARD_PORT ?= 8265
DASHBOARD_PID_FILE ?= run/dashboard_pf.pid

.PHONY: port-forward-dashboard
.SILENT: port-forward-dashboard
port-forward-dashboard: _ensure-tools
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Starting port-forward to Ray Dashboard on port $(DASHBOARD_PORT)$(RESET)"; \
	mkdir -p run logs; \
	if [ -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" ]; then \
	  OLD_PID=$$(cat "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" 2>/dev/null || true); \
	  if [ -n "$$OLD_PID" ] && ps -p "$$OLD_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Existing port-forward detected (PID=$$OLD_PID). Leaving it running.$(RESET)"; \
	    exit 0; \
	  fi; \
	fi; \
	HEAD_RES=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/node-type=head -o name | head -n1); \
	printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Using resource: $$HEAD_RES$(RESET)"; \
	if [ -z "$$HEAD_RES" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Could not find Ray head pod in namespace $(NAMESPACE)$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 1; \
	fi; \
	LOG_FILE=logs/portforward-dashboard-$(DASHBOARD_PORT).log; \
	nohup kubectl -n $(NAMESPACE) port-forward "$$HEAD_RES" $(DASHBOARD_PORT):$(DASHBOARD_PORT) --address 0.0.0.0 > "$$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 & \
	PF_PID=$$!; \
	echo "$$PF_PID" > "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	sleep 1; \
	if ps -p "$$PF_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward running (PID=$$PF_PID). Logs: $$LOG_FILE$(RESET)"; \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Access the dashboard at: http://127.0.0.1:$(DASHBOARD_PORT) or your host IP$(RESET)"; \
	else \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward failed to start. See $$LOG_FILE$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 1; \
	fi

.PHONY: port-forward-dashboard-stop
.SILENT: port-forward-dashboard-stop
port-forward-dashboard-stop:
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	if [ ! -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] No PID file found (nothing to stop)$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 0; \
	fi; \
	PID=$$(cat "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" 2>/dev/null || true); \
	if [ -z "$$PID" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] PID file empty (nothing to stop)$(RESET)"; \
	  rm -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	  exit 0; \
	fi; \
	if ps -p "$$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Stopping port-forward (PID=$$PID)$(RESET)"; \
	  kill "$$PID" || true; \
	  sleep 1; \
	  if ps -p "$$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Force killing PID $$PID$(RESET)"; \
	    kill -9 "$$PID" || true; \
	  fi; \
	else \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] No running process for PID $$PID$(RESET)"; \
	fi; \
	rm -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward stopped$(RESET)"

.PHONY: _detect-node-ip
_detect-node-ip:
	@if [ -z "$(NODE_IP)" ]; then \
	  DETECTED_IP=$$(ip route get 1.1.1.1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($$i=="src") {print $$(i+1); exit}}'); \
	  if [ -z "$$DETECTED_IP" ]; then \
	    echo "$(RED)$(BOLD)Unable to auto-detect NODE_IP; please pass NODE_IP=...$(RESET)"; \
	    exit 1; \
	  fi; \
	  echo "Using auto-detected NODE_IP=$$DETECTED_IP"; \
	  echo "NODE_IP=$$DETECTED_IP" > .make.cached.env; \
	else \
	  echo "NODE_IP=$(NODE_IP)" > .make.cached.env; \
	fi

.PHONY: redeploy-clean
redeploy-clean: _ensure-tools
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Deleting RayService $(SERVICE_NAME)$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl delete rayservice $(SERVICE_NAME) -n $(NAMESPACE) --ignore-not-found=true || true; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Waiting briefly for pods to terminate$(RESET)"; \
	sleep 3; \
	PODS=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes -o name 2>/dev/null || true); \
		if [ -n "$$PODS" ]; then \
			printf "%b\n" "Found lingering Ray pods, forcing deletion:"; printf "%b\n" "$$PODS"; \
	  kubectl delete $$PODS -n $(NAMESPACE) --force --grace-period=0 || true; \
	fi; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Verifying no Ray pods remain$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes || true; \
	if command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[redeploy-clean] Checking GPU processes$(RESET)"; \
	  nvidia-smi || true; \
	fi

.PHONY: deploy-apply
deploy-apply: _ensure-tools
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Applying $(RAYSERVICE_FILE)$(RESET)"; \
		kubectl apply -n $(NAMESPACE) -f $(RAYSERVICE_FILE); \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Waiting for Ray pods to appear$(RESET)"; \
	for i in $$(seq 1 60); do \
	  CNT=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes -o name 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '); \
			if [ "$$CNT" -gt 0 ]; then printf "%b\n" "Found $$CNT Ray pods"; break; fi; \
	  sleep 2; \
	done; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Waiting for Ray pods Ready (timeout 10m)$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl wait --for=condition=ready pod -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/is-ray-node=yes --timeout=600s; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Waiting for Serve endpoints to be ready$(RESET)"; \
	for i in $$(seq 1 150); do \
	  EP=$$(kubectl get endpoints $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[*].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
			if [ -n "$$EP" ]; then printf "%b\n" "Serve endpoints: $$EP"; break; fi; \
	  sleep 2; \
	done; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[deploy-apply] Ray pods Ready$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -o wide | sed -n '1,200p'

.PHONY: smoke-health
smoke-health: _ensure-tools _detect-node-ip
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		. ./.make.cached.env; \
		IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
		ENDPOINT_IP=http://$${NODE_IP}:$(NODE_PORT); \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Checking health via Ingress: $$ENDPOINT_IP/health (Host: $$HOST)$(RESET)"; \
		RESOLVE=$$(getent hosts $$HOST 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $$1}' | head -n1 || true); \
		if [ -n "$$RESOLVE" ] && [ "$$RESOLVE" != "$$NODE_IP" ]; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Warning: $$HOST resolves to $$RESOLVE, expected $$NODE_IP$(RESET)"; \
		fi; \
		CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
		RES=$$(curl -s -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
		printf "%b\n" "Health code: $$CODE body: $$RES"; \
		if [ "$$CODE" != "200" ] || ! echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Ingress not healthy (code=$$CODE), trying direct pod endpoint fallback$(RESET)"; \
			POD_IP=$$(kubectl get endpoints embedding-service-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
			if [ -n "$$POD_IP" ]; then \
				printf "%b\n" "Trying http://$$POD_IP:8000/health"; \
				CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://$$POD_IP:8000/health || true); \
				RES=$$(curl -s http://$$POD_IP:8000/health || true); \
				printf "%b\n" "Fallback code: $$CODE body: $$RES"; \
				if [ "$$CODE" != "200" ] || ! echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then \
					printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Fallback health also not healthy$(RESET)"; \
					exit 1; \
				fi; \
				printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Fallback OK; waiting up to $(INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS)s for Ingress to become healthy$(RESET)"; \
				START=$$(date +%s); OK=false; \
				while :; do \
				  CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
				  RES=$$(curl -s -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
				  if [ "$$CODE" = "200" ] && echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then OK=true; break; fi; \
				  NOW=$$(date +%s); ELAPSED=$$((NOW-START)); \
				  if [ "$$ELAPSED" -ge "$(INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS)" ]; then break; fi; \
				  sleep 2; \
				done; \
				if [ "$$OK" != "true" ]; then \
				  printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Ingress still not healthy after $(INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS)s (last code=$$CODE). Aborting.$(RESET)"; \
				  exit 1; \
				fi; \
			else \
				printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Could not determine pod IP for fallback$(RESET)"; \
				exit 1; \
			fi; \
		fi; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Health OK$(RESET)"

.PHONY: serve-status
.SILENT: serve-status
serve-status:
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	HEAD_POD=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/node-type=head -o name | head -n1 | cut -d/ -f2); \
	if [ -z "$$HEAD_POD" ]; then echo "No Ray head pod found"; exit 1; fi; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[serve-status] Querying Serve status from $$HEAD_POD$(RESET)"; \
	kubectl exec -n $(NAMESPACE) $$HEAD_POD -- python3 -c 'import json, dataclasses as dc; from ray import serve; s=serve.status(); d = s.to_dict() if hasattr(s, "to_dict") else dc.asdict(s); print(json.dumps(d, indent=2))'

.PHONY: quick-load-test
quick-load-test: _ensure-tools _detect-node-ip
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		. ./.make.cached.env; \
		IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
	TARGET_URL=http://$$HOST:$(NODE_PORT); \
	HEALTH_URL=http://$${NODE_IP}:$(NODE_PORT); \
	printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Debug: HOST=$$HOST TARGET_URL=$$TARGET_URL HEALTH_URL=$$HEALTH_URL$(RESET)"; \
	# Prefer ingress: health wait (skip if SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT=true)
	if [ "$${SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT:-false}" != "true" ]; then \
	  START=$$(date +%s); \
	  OK=false; \
	  while :; do \
	    CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$HEALTH_URL/health || true); \
	    RES=$$(curl -s -H "Host: $$HOST" $$HEALTH_URL/health || true); \
	    if [ "$$CODE" = "200" ] && echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then OK=true; break; fi; \
	    NOW=$$(date +%s); \
	    ELAPSED=$$((NOW-START)); \
	    if [ "$$ELAPSED" -ge "$(INGRESS_WAIT_SECS)" ]; then break; fi; \
	    sleep 2; \
	  done; \
	  if [ "$$OK" != "true" ]; then \
	    if [ "$(USE_INGRESS_ONLY)" = "true" ]; then \
	      printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Ingress not healthy after $(INGRESS_WAIT_SECS)s (last code=$$CODE). Aborting per USE_INGRESS_ONLY=true$(RESET)"; \
	      exit 1; \
	    else \
	      POD_IP=$$(kubectl get endpoints $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
	      if [ -n "$$POD_IP" ]; then \
	        TARGET_URL=http://$$POD_IP:8000; \
	        printf "%b\n" "Ingress not ready (last code=$$CODE), falling back to direct pod URL: $$TARGET_URL"; \
	      fi; \
	    fi; \
	  fi; \
	fi; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Running load test to $$TARGET_URL: R=$(TEST_REQUESTS) C=$(TEST_CONCURRENCY) segmentation=$(TEST_SEGMENTATION)$(RESET)"; \
	python3 working_dir/load_test.py --url $$TARGET_URL --requests $(TEST_REQUESTS) --concurrency $(TEST_CONCURRENCY) --segmentation $(TEST_SEGMENTATION)

.PHONY: quick-load-test-ingress
quick-load-test-ingress: smoke-health
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	. ./.make.cached.env; \
	IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
	URL=http://$$HOST:$(NODE_PORT); \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test-ingress] Running ingress-only load test: $$URL R=$(TEST_REQUESTS) C=$(TEST_CONCURRENCY) segmentation=$(TEST_SEGMENTATION)$(RESET)"; \
	python3 working_dir/load_test.py --url $$URL --requests $(TEST_REQUESTS) --concurrency $(TEST_CONCURRENCY) --segmentation $(TEST_SEGMENTATION)

.PHONY: redeploy
redeploy: redeploy-clean deploy-apply smoke-health
	@printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[redeploy] Completed cleanup, deploy, and health verification$(RESET)"

.PHONY: redeploy-and-test
redeploy-and-test: redeploy quick-load-test-ingress
	@printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[redeploy-and-test] Completed end-to-end redeploy with ingress load test$(RESET)"

.PHONY: redeploy-and-test-ingress
redeploy-and-test-ingress: redeploy quick-load-test-ingress
	@printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[redeploy-and-test-ingress] Completed end-to-end redeploy with ingress load test$(RESET)"

.PHONY: redeploy-and-test-fallback
redeploy-and-test-fallback: redeploy

	@printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[redeploy-and-test-fallback] Completed end-to-end redeploy with fallback load test$(RESET)"

**Analyzing deployment limits**

I'm looking at the worker setup where calculating 6+6 gives me 12. With 2 CPUs per replica, scheduling up to 6 replicas seems possible, so the CPU isn't the issue. The GPUs can't exceed 10 at 0.2 each, but why am I limited to only 2 replicas? It might relate to concurrency limits or deployment configurations. It seems like Ray Serve can't schedule more due to only 2 nodes available, especially since the head node lacks GPU resources for additional replicas.

**Understanding replica limitations**

With 2 workers, each having 1 GPU, the total GPU across the cluster is 2. Since each replica requires 0.2 GPU, one GPU can support up to 5 replicas, allowing for 10 replicas total with 2 GPUs. So, why are we only seeing 2 replicas? It might be due to the autoscaling configuration not engaging at startup, even though 'min_replicas' is set to 4. Without any load, the autoscaler seems to shrink back to the initial default, which is possibly leading to this unexpected behavior.

**Examining autoscaling configuration**

Another possibility is that our code is using '@serve.deployment' with an autoscaling configuration, but maybe not set up correctly for 'serve 2.x' semantics. In this version, the deployment options for 'autoscaling_config' include 'min_replicas', 'max_replicas', and 'initial_replicas'. However, 'serve.status()' shows just 2 replicas, which might be the system default due to fused configurations. I could try forcing 'num_replicas=4' to establish a fixed number. Since the user wants 4 replicas, I'll adjust the code accordingly, but I have to be cautious about the GPU budget too.

**Planning for deployment changes**

First, I need to choose the number of replicas. The deployment used by serveConfigV2 has a specific import path, and any changes made will require me to rebuild the Docker image and redeploy. The current image in the cluster is v4.0.2, and we haven't rebuilt it since making code edits. To change the serve settings, we definitely need to build and push, or we could use the Serve config to adjust the number of replicas. However, since serveConfigV2 only uses the import path without specifying options, rebuilding is necessary. The user requested to increase replicas and redeploy, so I’ll proceed with that. I'll bump the version to maybe v4.0.3, as it's currently pinned to v4.0.2, which isn't ideal.

**Updating version and deployment**

It looks like the 'version' file is currently at v4.0.2. If I run 'build-and-push-optimized', the version bump will just reset it to v4.0.2 again. The cluster image in YAML also references v4.0.2, and pushing it again will trigger 'imagePullPolicy: Always'. That works for the local cluster, and duplicating the tag in a development environment is fine. I need to make code modifications to set 'num_replicas=4' while possibly removing or nullifying 'autoscaling_config'. I'll verify the 'serve.deployment' signature to ensure 'num_replicas' is allowed. After that, I'll build, push, and redeploy the RayService manifest. Then, I'll check the status to confirm four replicas are running and conduct a quick load test.

"""
Ray Serve deployment wrapper for EmbeddingService.

This module wraps the existing FastAPI application with Ray Serve
decorators to enable distributed deployment with autoscaling and
load balancing. No changes to the existing application logic required.
"""

from ray import serve

# Import the existing FastAPI app
from src.service.main import app


@serve.deployment(
    name="embedding-service",
    ray_actor_options={
        "num_cpus": 2,
        "num_gpus": 0.2,  # Allow 2-5 replicas per GPU depending on model size
    },
    # Increased per-replica concurrency to coordinate with optimized semaphore limits.
    # Fixed 4 replicas to satisfy the request deterministically.
    max_ongoing_requests=200,
    num_replicas=4,
)
@serve.ingress(app)
class EmbeddingServiceDeployment:
    """
    Ray Serve deployment that wraps the FastAPI application.
    
    The @serve.ingress decorator makes all FastAPI routes available
    through Ray Serve, preserving all existing endpoints, middleware,
    and business logic without modification.
    """
    pass


# Deployment binding for Ray Serve
deployment = EmbeddingServiceDeployment.bind()

## What I changed

- Scaled Serve replicas to 4 deterministically
  - Updated

to use a fixed replica count:
    - Replaced autoscaling with `num_replicas=4` so four replicas are started immediately.
- Kept GPU workers at 2
  - Reverted worker group back to `replicas: 2` in

to match available GPUs and avoid Pending Pods.
- Stabilized ingress after fallback
  - Hardened `smoke-health` to, after a successful pod fallback, wait until the ingress itself returns HTTP 200 with healthy JSON (up to 90s). This removes the immediate 503 window after deploy.
- Added a quick status tool
  - New Make target `serve-status` uses `kubectl exec` into the head pod to print Serve status JSON (including replica counts).

## Actions run and results

- Built and pushed the updated image (tag stays v4.0.2; imagePullPolicy is Always).
- Redeployed:
  - Head and two worker pods up and Ready.

- Verified replicas:
  - `make serve-status` shows replica_states RUNNING: 4 for deployment `embedding-service`.

## How to use

- End-to-end scale to 4, redeploy, wait for ingress, and test:

- Check Serve deployment status (including replicas):

- We used a fixed replica count to satisfy “increase to 4” precisely. If you prefer autoscaling instead (with min/initial replicas), we can restore autoscaling and use load to scale up; I’ll keep the ingress stabilization either way.

: improved `smoke-health` to wait for ingress after fallback; added `serve-status`.

.PHONY: port-forward-dashboard
.SILENT: port-forward-dashboard

	@set -euo pipefail; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Starting port-forward to Ray Dashboard on port $(DASHBOARD_PORT)$(RESET)"; \
	mkdir -p run logs; \
	if [ -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" ]; then \
	  OLD_PID=$$(cat "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" 2>/dev/null || true); \
	  if [ -n "$$OLD_PID" ] && ps -p "$$OLD_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Existing port-forward detected (PID=$$OLD_PID). Leaving it running.$(RESET)"; \
	    exit 0; \
	  fi; \
	fi; \
	HEAD_RES=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/node-type=head -o name | head -n1); \
	printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Using resource: $$HEAD_RES$(RESET)"; \
	if [ -z "$$HEAD_RES" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Could not find Ray head pod in namespace $(NAMESPACE)$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 1; \
	fi; \
	LOG_FILE=logs/portforward-dashboard-$(DASHBOARD_PORT).log; \
	nohup kubectl -n $(NAMESPACE) port-forward "$$HEAD_RES" $(DASHBOARD_PORT):$(DASHBOARD_PORT) --address 0.0.0.0 > "$$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 & \
	PF_PID=$$!; \
	echo "$$PF_PID" > "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	sleep 1; \
	if ps -p "$$PF_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward running (PID=$$PF_PID). Logs: $$LOG_FILE$(RESET)"; \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Access the dashboard at: http://127.0.0.1:$(DASHBOARD_PORT) or your host IP$(RESET)"; \
	else \

	  exit 1; \
	fi

.PHONY: port-forward-dashboard-stop
.SILENT: port-forward-dashboard-stop
port-forward-dashboard-stop:
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	if [ ! -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] No PID file found (nothing to stop)$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 0; \
	fi; \
	PID=$$(cat "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" 2>/dev/null || true); \
	if [ -z "$$PID" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] PID file empty (nothing to stop)$(RESET)"; \
	  rm -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	  exit 0; \
	fi; \
	if ps -p "$$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Stopping port-forward (PID=$$PID)$(RESET)"; \
	  kill "$$PID" || true; \
	  sleep 1; \
	  if ps -p "$$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Force killing PID $$PID$(RESET)"; \
	    kill -9 "$$PID" || true; \
	  fi; \
	else \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] No running process for PID $$PID$(RESET)"; \
	fi; \
	rm -f "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Port-forward stopped$(RESET)"

.PHONY: _detect-node-ip

	@if [ -z "$(NODE_IP)" ]; then \

	kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -o wide | sed -n '1,200p'

edits.text:
## Build → Redeploy → Test: Make-driven playbook

This guide explains how to build, redeploy, and test the Embedding Service using the Makefile, with clear options, parameterization, and visual diagrams of the flow. It covers ingress health behavior, fallback logic, and verification tools (like replica counts and dashboard access).

### What you’ll get
- One-command build-and-push of the Docker image
- One-command redeploy with ingress health checks and load testing
- Tunable parameters for concurrency, ingress behavior, and timeouts
- Diagrams: sequence, flowchart (health/fallback), and component topology (UML-style)


## Targets at a glance

| Target | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `build-and-push-optimized` | Bump version (pinned), build Docker image, push `:version` and `:latest` tags. |
| `redeploy` | Clean RayService + pods, apply manifest, wait Ready, verify health (ingress with fallback+stabilization). |
| `redeploy-and-test` | Redeploy then run ingress-only load test. |
| `redeploy-and-test-ingress` | Same as above, explicit name. |
| `redeploy-and-test-fallback` | Redeploy then run load test allowing fallback to direct pod URL. |
| `smoke-health` | Health probe: tries ingress first, falls back to a pod, then waits for ingress to become healthy. |
| `quick-load-test-ingress` | Ingress-only load test (depends on `smoke-health`). |
| `quick-load-test` | Load test preferring ingress; optionally falls back to pod if configured. |
| `serve-status` | Prints Ray Serve application/deployment status (including replica counts) from the head pod. |
| `port-forward-dashboard` | Starts Ray dashboard port-forward on 8265 in background; prints PID and log. |
| `port-forward-dashboard-stop` | Stops the background dashboard port-forward. |


## Key parameters

Override at invocation: `make <target> KEY=value`

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| `REGISTRY` | `192.168.1.3:5000` | Local registry for pushing images |
| `IMAGE_NAME` | `embedding-service` | Image repo name |
| `VERSION_FILE` | `version` | Read tag from this file |
| `SERVICE_NAME` | `embedding-service` | K8s RayService name |
| `RAYSERVICE_FILE` | `k8s/rayservice-local.yaml` | RayService manifest path |
| `NAMESPACE` | `default` | K8s namespace |
| `NODE_PORT` | `30333` | NodePort that the ingress listens on |
| `TEST_REQUESTS` | `200` | Total number of requests for load tests |
| `TEST_CONCURRENCY` | `10` | Concurrent workers for load tests |
| `TEST_SEGMENTATION` | `false` | Enable request segmentation in load tester |
| `USE_INGRESS_ONLY` | `true` | If true, abort tests when ingress isn’t healthy (no fallback) |
| `INGRESS_WAIT_SECS` | `60` | Wait time for ingress to become healthy in quick load test |
| `INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS` | `90` | Additional wait for ingress after a successful pod fallback in `smoke-health` |


## Typical flows

### Build and push image
- `make build-and-push-optimized`
  - Bumps the pinned version file (stays the same if already set)
  - Builds the Docker image and pushes both `:version` and `:latest`

### Redeploy and test via ingress
- `make redeploy-and-test` (same as `redeploy-and-test-ingress`)
  - Cleans prior RayService + pods; reapplies manifest
  - Waits for Ray pods Ready and Serve endpoints to appear
  - Runs `smoke-health` which:
    1) Checks ingress `GET /health` with Host header
    2) If 503/unhealthy, falls back to one Serve pod `GET /health`
    3) If fallback is healthy, waits up to `INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS` for ingress to become healthy
  - Runs a small ingress-only load test using `working_dir/load_test.py`

### Redeploy and test with fallback allowed
- `make redeploy-and-test-fallback`
  - Same redeploy steps as above
  - Runs `quick-load-test` with `USE_INGRESS_ONLY=false` and `SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT=true`
  - If ingress isn’t ready, it falls back to a direct pod URL


## Health and fallback logic (flowchart)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Start smoke-health] --> B[Compute HOST embeddings.<ip>.nip.io and ENDPOINT_IP http://<node_ip>:<node_port>]
    B --> C{Ingress /health returns 200 and status=healthy?}
    C -- Yes --> D[Health OK]
    C -- No --> E[Get a Serve pod IP via embedding-service-serve-svc endpoints]
    E --> F{Pod /health returns 200 and status=healthy?}
    F -- No --> G[Fail: Fallback health not healthy]
    F -- Yes --> H[Fallback OK]
    H --> I[Wait up to INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS for ingress to return healthy]
    I --> J{Ingress healthy within window?}
    J -- No --> K[Fail: Ingress still not healthy]
    J -- Yes --> D
```


## End-to-end sequence (redeploy-and-test)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Dev as Developer
    participant Make as Makefile
    participant Kube as Kubernetes API
    participant Ray as Ray Cluster
    participant Ingress as NGINX Ingress
    participant Service as Serve Service (embedding-service-serve-svc)

    Dev->>Make: make redeploy-and-test
    Make->>Kube: delete RayService + lingering pods
    Make->>Kube: apply rayservice-local.yaml
    Make->>Kube: wait pods Ready (head + workers)
    Make->>Ray: wait Serve endpoints appear
    Make->>Ingress: health check with Host header
    alt ingress healthy
        Make->>Dev: Health OK
    else ingress 503/unhealthy
        Make->>Service: fallback health via pod IP
        Service-->>Make: 200 healthy
        Make->>Ingress: wait for ingress healthy (post-fallback window)
        Ingress-->>Make: 200 healthy
    end
    Make->>Make: run quick-load-test-ingress (urllib client)
    Make-->>Dev: Summary (counts, mean, p50, p95, p99)
```


## Component topology (UML-style)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Client((Client))
  Proxy[External NGINX Proxy (optional)]
  Ingress[Cluster NGINX Ingress (NodePort 30333)]
  SVC[(embedding-service-serve-svc)]
  subgraph Ray Serve
    direction TB
    ProxyEvery[Serve HTTP Proxies (EveryNode)]
    Rep1[EmbeddingService replica 1]
    Rep2[EmbeddingService replica 2]
    Rep3[EmbeddingService replica 3]
    Rep4[EmbeddingService replica 4]
  end

  Client -->|HTTP| Proxy
  Proxy -->|Host: embeddings.<ip>.nip.io| Ingress
  Ingress -->|ClusterIP:8000| SVC
  SVC --> ProxyEvery
  ProxyEvery --> Rep1
  ProxyEvery --> Rep2
  ProxyEvery --> Rep3
  ProxyEvery --> Rep4
```


## Practical tips and parametrization

- Use ingress-only tests for steady-state verification:
  - `make quick-load-test-ingress TEST_REQUESTS=50 TEST_CONCURRENCY=5`
- Use fallback tests during bring-up or when iterating cluster config:
  - `make redeploy-and-test-fallback`
- Tweak ingress stabilization time if your ingress is slower to attach routes:
  - `make smoke-health INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS=120`
- Control load intensity:
  - `make quick-load-test-ingress TEST_REQUESTS=500 TEST_CONCURRENCY=50`
- Check Serve replicas and proxy health quickly:
  - `make serve-status`
- Ray dashboard (optional):
  - Start: `make port-forward-dashboard`
  - Stop: `make port-forward-dashboard-stop`
  - Then browse `http://127.0.0.1:8265`


## Troubleshooting

- 503 after deploy:
  - This is typically ingress warm-up. `smoke-health` now waits for ingress to become healthy after verifying a pod fallback, preventing immediate test failures. If it persists, check ingress controller logs and service endpoints.
- nip.io mismatch:
  - The Makefile warns if `embeddings.<ip>.nip.io` resolves to a different IP than expected. Ensure the Host header and Node IP align with your ingress rule.
- Pending worker pods:
  - If you raise worker replicas beyond available GPUs, pods may stay Pending. Keep `workerGroupSpecs.replicas` ≤ GPU count, or adjust scheduling/resources.
- Serve replicas vs. autoscaling:
  - You can fix replicas (e.g., 4) or use autoscaling. If you prefer autoscaling, ensure `min_replicas` and `initial_replicas` are set appropriately in the deployment configuration and the cluster has resources to scale.

- HTTP 200
- JSON body includes `{"status": "healthy"}` (case-insensitive check)
- Host header routing via `embeddings.<ip>.nip.io` against NodeIP:NodePort
- Fallback to a live Serve pod, then a timed wait for ingress to become healthy

- RayService manifest: `k8s/rayservice-local.yaml`
- Load test client: `working_dir/load_test.py`
- Serve deployment wrapper: `src/service/ray_deployment.py`

.PHONY: port-forward-dashboard
.SILENT: port-forward-dashboard

	@set -euo pipefail; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Starting port-forward to Ray Dashboard on port $(DASHBOARD_PORT)$(RESET)"; \
	mkdir -p run logs; \

	  OLD_PID=$$(cat "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)" 2>/dev/null || true); \
	  if [ -n "$$OLD_PID" ] && ps -p "$$OLD_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Existing port-forward detected (PID=$$OLD_PID). Leaving it running.$(RESET)"; \
	    exit 0; \

	HEAD_RES=$$(kubectl get pods -n $(NAMESPACE) -l ray.io/node-type=head -o name | head -n1); \

	if [ -z "$$HEAD_RES" ]; then \
	  printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[dashboard] Could not find Ray head pod in namespace $(NAMESPACE)$(RESET)"; \
	  exit 1; \
	fi; \
	LOG_FILE=logs/portforward-dashboard-$(DASHBOARD_PORT).log; \

	PF_PID=$$!; \
	echo "$$PF_PID" > "$(DASHBOARD_PID_FILE)"; \
	sleep 1; \
	if ps -p "$$PF_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \

.PHONY: smoke-health
smoke-health: _ensure-tools _detect-node-ip
		@set -euo pipefail; \
		. ./.make.cached.env; \
		IP_DASH=$${NODE_IP//./-}; HOST=embeddings.$$IP_DASH.nip.io; \
		ENDPOINT_IP=http://$${NODE_IP}:$(NODE_PORT); \
		printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Checking health via Ingress: $$ENDPOINT_IP/health (Host: $$HOST)$(RESET)"; \
		RESOLVE=$$(getent hosts $$HOST 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $$1}' | head -n1 || true); \
		if [ -n "$$RESOLVE" ] && [ "$$RESOLVE" != "$$NODE_IP" ]; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Warning: $$HOST resolves to $$RESOLVE, expected $$NODE_IP$(RESET)"; \
		fi; \
		CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
		RES=$$(curl -s -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
		printf "%b\n" "Health code: $$CODE body: $$RES"; \
		if [ "$$CODE" != "200" ] || ! echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then \
			printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Ingress not healthy (code=$$CODE), trying direct pod endpoint fallback$(RESET)"; \
			POD_IP=$$(kubectl get endpoints embedding-service-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
			if [ -n "$$POD_IP" ]; then \
				printf "%b\n" "Trying http://$$POD_IP:8000/health"; \
				CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://$$POD_IP:8000/health || true); \
				RES=$$(curl -s http://$$POD_IP:8000/health || true); \
				printf "%b\n" "Fallback code: $$CODE body: $$RES"; \
				if [ "$$CODE" != "200" ] || ! echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then \
					printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Fallback health also not healthy$(RESET)"; \
					exit 1; \
				fi; \
				printf "%b\n" "$(BLUE)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Fallback OK; waiting up to $(INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS)s for Ingress to become healthy$(RESET)"; \
				START=$$(date +%s); OK=false; \
				while :; do \
				  CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
				  RES=$$(curl -s -H "Host: $$HOST" $$ENDPOINT_IP/health || true); \
				  if [ "$$CODE" = "200" ] && echo "$$RES" | grep -qi '"status"\s*:\s*"healthy"'; then OK=true; break; fi; \
				  NOW=$$(date +%s); ELAPSED=$$((NOW-START)); \
				  if [ "$$ELAPSED" -ge "$(INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS)" ]; then break; fi; \
				  sleep 2; \
				done; \
				if [ "$$OK" != "true" ]; then \
				  printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Ingress still not healthy after $(INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS)s (last code=$$CODE). Aborting.$(RESET)"; \
				  exit 1; \
				fi; \
			else \
				printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Could not determine pod IP for fallback$(RESET)"; \
				exit 1; \
			fi; \
		fi; \
		printf "%b\n" "$(GREEN)$(BOLD)[smoke-health] Health OK$(RESET)"

	@set -euo pipefail; \

		@set -euo pipefail; \

	if [ "$${SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT:-false}" != "true" ]; then \
	  START=$$(date +%s); \

	    CODE=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Host: $$HOST" $$HEALTH_URL/health || true); \

	    NOW=$$(date +%s); \
	    ELAPSED=$$((NOW-START)); \
	    if [ "$$ELAPSED" -ge "$(INGRESS_WAIT_SECS)" ]; then break; fi; \
	    sleep 2; \
	  done; \
	  if [ "$$OK" != "true" ]; then \
	    if [ "$(USE_INGRESS_ONLY)" = "true" ]; then \
	      printf "%b\n" "$(RED)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Ingress not healthy after $(INGRESS_WAIT_SECS)s (last code=$$CODE). Aborting per USE_INGRESS_ONLY=true$(RESET)"; \
	      exit 1; \
	    else \
	      POD_IP=$$(kubectl get endpoints $(SERVICE_NAME)-serve-svc -n $(NAMESPACE) -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true); \
	      if [ -n "$$POD_IP" ]; then \
	        TARGET_URL=http://$$POD_IP:8000; \
	        printf "%b\n" "Ingress not ready (last code=$$CODE), falling back to direct pod URL: $$TARGET_URL"; \
	      fi; \
	    fi; \
	  fi; \
	fi; \
	printf "%b\n" "$(YELLOW)$(BOLD)[quick-load-test] Running load test to $$TARGET_URL: R=$(TEST_REQUESTS) C=$(TEST_CONCURRENCY) segmentation=$(TEST_SEGMENTATION)$(RESET)"; \
	python3 working_dir/load_test.py --url $$TARGET_URL --requests $(TEST_REQUESTS) --concurrency $(TEST_CONCURRENCY) --segmentation $(TEST_SEGMENTATION)

children.text: This guide explains how to build, redeploy, and test the Embedding Service using the Makefile, with clear options, parameterization, and visual diagrams of the flow. It covers ingress health behavior, fallback logic, and verification tools (like replica counts and dashboard access).
- One-command build-and-push of the Docker image
- One-command redeploy with ingress health checks and load testing
- Tunable parameters for concurrency, ingress behavior, and timeouts
- Diagrams: sequence, flowchart (health/fallback), and component topology (UML-style)
| `build-and-push-optimized` | Bump version (pinned), build Docker image, push `:version` and `:latest` tags. |
| `redeploy` | Clean RayService + pods, apply manifest, wait Ready, verify health (ingress with fallback+stabilization). |
| `redeploy-and-test` | Redeploy then run ingress-only load test. |
| `redeploy-and-test-fallback` | Redeploy then run load test allowing fallback to direct pod URL. |
| `smoke-health` | Health probe: tries ingress first, falls back to a pod, then waits for ingress to become healthy. |

## Build → Redeploy → Test: Make-driven playbook

This guide explains how to build, redeploy, and test the Embedding Service using the Makefile, with clear options, parameterization, and visual diagrams of the flow. It covers ingress health behavior, fallback logic, and verification tools (like replica counts and dashboard access).

### What you’ll get
- One-command build-and-push of the Docker image
- One-command redeploy with ingress health checks and load testing
- Tunable parameters for concurrency, ingress behavior, and timeouts
- Diagrams: sequence, flowchart (health/fallback), and component topology (UML-style)


## Targets at a glance

| Target | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `build-and-push-optimized` | Bump version (pinned), build Docker image, push `:version` and `:latest` tags. |
| `redeploy` | Clean RayService + pods, apply manifest, wait Ready, verify health (ingress with fallback+stabilization). |
| `redeploy-and-test` | Redeploy then run ingress-only load test. |
| `redeploy-and-test-ingress` | Same as above, explicit name. |
| `redeploy-and-test-fallback` | Redeploy then run load test allowing fallback to direct pod URL. |
| `smoke-health` | Health probe: tries ingress first, falls back to a pod, then waits for ingress to become healthy. |
| `quick-load-test-ingress` | Ingress-only load test (depends on `smoke-health`). |
| `quick-load-test` | Load test preferring ingress; optionally falls back to pod if configured. |
| `serve-status` | Prints Ray Serve application/deployment status (including replica counts) from the head pod. |
| `port-forward-dashboard` | Starts Ray dashboard port-forward on 8265 in background; prints PID and log. |
| `port-forward-dashboard-stop` | Stops the background dashboard port-forward. |


## Key parameters

Override at invocation: `make <target> KEY=value`

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| `REGISTRY` | `192.168.1.3:5000` | Local registry for pushing images |
| `IMAGE_NAME` | `embedding-service` | Image repo name |
| `VERSION_FILE` | `version` | Read tag from this file |
| `SERVICE_NAME` | `embedding-service` | K8s RayService name |
| `RAYSERVICE_FILE` | `k8s/rayservice-local.yaml` | RayService manifest path |
| `NAMESPACE` | `default` | K8s namespace |
| `NODE_PORT` | `30333` | NodePort that the ingress listens on |
| `TEST_REQUESTS` | `200` | Total number of requests for load tests |
| `TEST_CONCURRENCY` | `10` | Concurrent workers for load tests |
| `TEST_SEGMENTATION` | `false` | Enable request segmentation in load tester |
| `USE_INGRESS_ONLY` | `true` | If true, abort tests when ingress isn’t healthy (no fallback) |
| `INGRESS_WAIT_SECS` | `60` | Wait time for ingress to become healthy in quick load test |

    - Stop: `make port-forward-dashboard-stop`

  # One-off registry override

  ### smoke-health
  - What it does
    - Checks ingress `GET /health` with Host header, falls back to a Serve pod if needed,

  ## Host header routing and manual checks

  Your ingress matches on the Host `embeddings.<ip>.nip.io`. Even when you hit the ingress by Node IP and port, you must send the Host header for routing.

  ### Quick curl checks
  ```bash
  # Substitute your NODE_IP and NODE_PORT if different
  NODE_IP=192.168.1.3
  NODE_PORT=30333
  HOST=embeddings.${NODE_IP//./-}.nip.io

  # Health via ingress (Host header required)
  curl -s -H "Host: $HOST" http://$NODE_IP:$NODE_PORT/health

  # Direct pod (bypasses ingress) — pick one IP from Serve endpoints
  POD_IP=$(kubectl get endpoints embedding-service-serve-svc -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}')
  curl -s http://$POD_IP:8000/health
  ```


  ## External proxy in front of ingress (optional)

  If you run an external NGINX proxy in front of Kubernetes ingress, preserve the Host header to match the ingress rule and forward to NodePort.

  ```nginx
  server {
    listen 80;
    server_name embeddings-proxy.local; # your proxy host

    client_max_body_size 20m;

    location / {
      # Upstream ingress
      proxy_pass http://192.168.1.3:30333;  # NODE_IP:NODE_PORT

      # Host header used by ingress routing
      proxy_set_header Host embeddings.192-168-1-3.nip.io;

      proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
      proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
      proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;

      proxy_http_version 1.1;
      proxy_set_header Connection "";
      proxy_buffering on;
      proxy_buffers 16 64k;
      proxy_buffer_size 64k;
      proxy_read_timeout 180s;
      proxy_send_timeout 180s;
      proxy_next_upstream error timeout http_500 http_502 http_503 http_504 invalid_header;
      proxy_next_upstream_tries 2;
    }
  }
  ```

+POD_IP=$(kubectl get endpoints embedding-service-serve-svc -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}')
+curl -s http://$POD_IP:8000/health
+```
+
+
+## External proxy in front of ingress (optional)
+
+If you run an external NGINX proxy in front of Kubernetes ingress, preserve the Host header to match the ingress rule and forward to NodePort.
+
+```nginx
+server {
+  listen 80;
+  server_name embeddings-proxy.local; # your proxy host
+
+  client_max_body_size 20m;
+
+  location / {
+    # Upstream ingress
+    proxy_pass http://192.168.1.3:30333;  # NODE_IP:NODE_PORT
+
+    # Host header used by ingress routing
+    proxy_set_header Host embeddings.192-168-1-3.nip.io;
+
+    proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
+    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
+    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
+
+    proxy_http_version 1.1;
+    proxy_set_header Connection "";
+    proxy_buffering on;
+    proxy_buffers 16 64k;
+    proxy_buffer_size 64k;
+    proxy_read_timeout 180s;
+    proxy_send_timeout 180s;
+    proxy_next_upstream error timeout http_500 http_502 http_503 http_504 invalid_header;
+    proxy_next_upstream_tries 2;
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Tip: parameterize the upstream and Host if you deploy this across environments.
+
+
+## Parameter quick reference by target
+
+| Target | Primary variables |
+|---|---|
+| build-and-push-optimized | REGISTRY, IMAGE_NAME, VERSION_FILE |
+| smoke-health | NODE_PORT, NAMESPACE, INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS |
+| quick-load-test-ingress | TEST_REQUESTS, TEST_CONCURRENCY, TEST_SEGMENTATION |
+| quick-load-test | USE_INGRESS_ONLY, INGRESS_WAIT_SECS, SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT, TEST_* |
+| redeploy | RAYSERVICE_FILE, NAMESPACE, SERVICE_NAME |
+| redeploy-and-test(-ingress) | TEST_REQUESTS, TEST_CONCURRENCY |
+| redeploy-and-test-fallback | TEST_REQUESTS, TEST_CONCURRENCY (and uses USE_INGRESS_ONLY=false, SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT=true) |
+| serve-status | NAMESPACE |
+| port-forward-dashboard(-stop) | DASHBOARD_PORT (fixed in Makefile), NAMESPACE |
+
+
+## CI/CD quick examples
+
+```bash
+# Build and push (pre-deploy job)
+make build-and-push-optimized REGISTRY=$CI_REGISTRY
+
+# Apply manifest then ingress-only test
+make redeploy-and-test TEST_REQUESTS=100 TEST_CONCURRENCY=10
+
+# Faster smoke-only check without load
+make smoke-health INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS=60
+```
+
+
+## Troubleshooting
+
+- 503 after deploy:
+  - This is typically ingress warm-up. `smoke-health` now waits for ingress to become healthy after verifying a pod fallback, preventing immediate test failures. If it persists, check ingress controller logs and service endpoints.
+- nip.io mismatch:
+  - The Makefile warns if `embeddings.<ip>.nip.io` resolves to a different IP than expected. Ensure the Host header and Node IP align with your ingress rule.
+- Pending worker pods:
+  - If you raise worker replicas beyond available GPUs, pods may stay Pending. Keep `workerGroupSpecs.replicas` ≤ GPU count, or adjust scheduling/resources.
+- Serve replicas vs. autoscaling:
+  - You can fix replicas (e.g., 4) or use autoscaling. If you prefer autoscaling, ensure `min_replicas` and `initial_replicas` are set appropriately in the deployment configuration and the cluster has resources to scale.
+
+

### Redeploy and test via ingress
- `make redeploy-and-test` (same as `redeploy-and-test-ingress`)
  - Cleans prior RayService + pods; reapplies manifest
  - Waits for Ray pods Ready and Serve endpoints to appear
  - Runs `smoke-health` which:

    2) If 503/unhealthy, falls back to one Serve pod `GET /health`
    3) If fallback is healthy, waits up to `INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS` for ingress to become healthy
  - Runs a small ingress-only load test using `working_dir/load_test.py`

### Redeploy and test with fallback allowed
- `make redeploy-and-test-fallback`
  - Same redeploy steps as above
  - Runs `quick-load-test` with `USE_INGRESS_ONLY=false` and `SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT=true`
  - If ingress isn't ready, it falls back to a direct pod URL


## Health and fallback logic (flowchart)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Start smoke-health] --> B[Compute HOST embeddings.<ip>.nip.io and ENDPOINT_IP http://<node_ip>:<node_port>]
    B --> C{Ingress /health returns 200 and status=healthy?}
    C -- Yes --> D[Health OK]
    C -- No --> E[Get a Serve pod IP via embedding-service-serve-svc endpoints]
    E --> F{Pod /health returns 200 and status=healthy?}
    F -- No --> G[Fail: Fallback health not healthy]
    F -- Yes --> H[Fallback OK]
    H --> I[Wait up to INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS for ingress to return healthy]
    I --> J{Ingress healthy within window?}
    J -- No --> K[Fail: Ingress still not healthy]
    J -- Yes --> D
```


## End-to-end sequence (redeploy-and-test)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Dev as Developer
    participant Make as Makefile
    participant Kube as Kubernetes API
    participant Ray as Ray Cluster
    participant Ingress as NGINX Ingress
    participant Service as Serve Service (embedding-service-serve-svc)

    Dev->>Make: make redeploy-and-test
    Make->>Kube: delete RayService + lingering pods
    Make->>Kube: apply rayservice-local.yaml
    Make->>Kube: wait pods Ready (head + workers)
    Make->>Ray: wait Serve endpoints appear
    Make->>Ingress: health check with Host header
    alt ingress healthy
        Make->>Dev: Health OK
    else ingress 503/unhealthy
        Make->>Service: fallback health via pod IP
        Service-->>Make: 200 healthy
        Make->>Ingress: wait for ingress healthy (post-fallback window)
        Ingress-->>Make: 200 healthy
    end
    Make->>Make: run quick-load-test-ingress (urllib client)
    Make-->>Dev: Summary (counts, mean, p50, p95, p99)
```

## Build → Redeploy → Test: Make-driven playbook

This guide explains how to build, redeploy, and test the Embedding Service using the Makefile, with clear options, parameterization, and visual diagrams of the flow. It covers ingress health behavior, fallback logic, and verification tools (like replica counts and dashboard access).

### What you’ll get
- One-command build-and-push of the Docker image
- One-command redeploy with ingress health checks and load testing
- Tunable parameters for concurrency, ingress behavior, and timeouts
- Diagrams: sequence, flowchart (health/fallback), and component topology (UML-style)


## Targets at a glance

| Target | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `build-and-push-optimized` | Bump version (pinned), build Docker image, push `:version` and `:latest` tags. |
| `redeploy` | Clean RayService + pods, apply manifest, wait Ready, verify health (ingress with fallback+stabilization). |
| `redeploy-and-test` | Redeploy then run ingress-only load test. |
| `redeploy-and-test-ingress` | Same as above, explicit name. |
| `redeploy-and-test-fallback` | Redeploy then run load test allowing fallback to direct pod URL. |
| `smoke-health` | Health probe: tries ingress first, falls back to a pod, then waits for ingress to become healthy. |
| `quick-load-test-ingress` | Ingress-only load test (depends on `smoke-health`). |
| `quick-load-test` | Load test preferring ingress; optionally falls back to pod if configured. |
| `serve-status` | Prints Ray Serve application/deployment status (including replica counts) from the head pod. |
| `port-forward-dashboard` | Starts Ray dashboard port-forward on 8265 in background; prints PID and log. |
| `port-forward-dashboard-stop` | Stops the background dashboard port-forward. |


## Key parameters

Override at invocation: `make <target> KEY=value`

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| `REGISTRY` | `192.168.1.3:5000` | Local registry for pushing images |
| `IMAGE_NAME` | `embedding-service` | Image repo name |
| `VERSION_FILE` | `version` | Read tag from this file |
| `SERVICE_NAME` | `embedding-service` | K8s RayService name |
| `RAYSERVICE_FILE` | `k8s/rayservice-local.yaml` | RayService manifest path |
| `NAMESPACE` | `default` | K8s namespace |
| `NODE_PORT` | `30333` | NodePort that the ingress listens on |
| `TEST_REQUESTS` | `200` | Total number of requests for load tests |
| `TEST_CONCURRENCY` | `10` | Concurrent workers for load tests |
| `TEST_SEGMENTATION` | `false` | Enable request segmentation in load tester |
| `USE_INGRESS_ONLY` | `true` | If true, abort tests when ingress isn’t healthy (no fallback) |
| `INGRESS_WAIT_SECS` | `60` | Wait time for ingress to become healthy in quick load test |
| `INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS` | `90` | Additional wait for ingress after a successful pod fallback in `smoke-health` |


## Typical flows

### Build and push image
- `make build-and-push-optimized`
  - Bumps the pinned version file (stays the same if already set)
  - Builds the Docker image and pushes both `:version` and `:latest`

### Redeploy and test via ingress
- `make redeploy-and-test` (same as `redeploy-and-test-ingress`)
  ## Practical tips and parametrization

  - Use ingress-only tests for steady-state verification:
    - `make quick-load-test-ingress TEST_REQUESTS=50 TEST_CONCURRENCY=5`
  - Use fallback tests during bring-up or when iterating cluster config:
    - `make redeploy-and-test-fallback`
  - Tweak ingress stabilization time if your ingress is slower to attach routes:
    - `make smoke-health INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS=120`
  - Control load intensity:
    - `make quick-load-test-ingress TEST_REQUESTS=500 TEST_CONCURRENCY=50`
  - Check Serve replicas and proxy health quickly:
    - `make serve-status`
  - Ray dashboard (optional):
    - Start: `make port-forward-dashboard`
    - Stop: `make port-forward-dashboard-stop`
    - Then browse `http://127.0.0.1:8265`


  ## Hands-on recipes by target (with directives and examples)

  Below are practical, copyable examples tied to specific Makefile targets and variables.

  ### build-and-push-optimized
  - What it does
    - Sequences `version-bump` → `docker-build` → `docker-push`.
    - Produces and pushes `$(REGISTRY)/$(IMAGE_NAME):$(VERSION)` and `:latest`.
  - Key directives and variables
    - Targets: `version-bump`, `docker-build`, `docker-push`
    - Vars: `REGISTRY`, `IMAGE_NAME`, `VERSION_FILE`, `FULL_IMAGE_TAG`
  - Examples
  ```bash
  # Build and push with defaults
  make build-and-push-optimized

  # One-off registry override
  make build-and-push-optimized REGISTRY=10.0.0.5:5000
  ```

  ### smoke-health
  - What it does
    - Checks ingress `GET /health` with Host header, falls back to a Serve pod if needed,
      then waits up to `INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS` for ingress to become healthy.
  - Key directives and variables
    - Strict shell: `set -euo pipefail`
    - Vars: `NODE_PORT`, `NAMESPACE`, `INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS`
  - Examples
  ```bash
  # Basic health check
  make smoke-health

  # Extend the post-fallback wait window
  make smoke-health INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS=120
  ```

  ### quick-load-test-ingress
  - What it does
    - Depends on `smoke-health`; runs urllib client to ingress URL only.
  - Key variables
    - `TEST_REQUESTS`, `TEST_CONCURRENCY`, `TEST_SEGMENTATION`
  - Examples
  ```bash
  # Sanity run
  make quick-load-test-ingress TEST_REQUESTS=50 TEST_CONCURRENCY=5

  # Heavier run
  make quick-load-test-ingress TEST_REQUESTS=1000 TEST_CONCURRENCY=50
  ```

  ### quick-load-test
  - What it does
    - Prefers ingress; can fall back to a direct pod URL when `USE_INGRESS_ONLY=false`.
  - Key variables
    - `USE_INGRESS_ONLY`, `INGRESS_WAIT_SECS`, `SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT`
  - Examples
  ```bash
  # Allow fallback to direct pod URL
  make quick-load-test USE_INGRESS_ONLY=false TEST_REQUESTS=200 TEST_CONCURRENCY=20

  # Skip pre-test health wait (useful during active iteration)
  make quick-load-test SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT=true TEST_REQUESTS=100 TEST_CONCURRENCY=10
  ```

  ### redeploy
  - What it does
    - `redeploy-clean` → `deploy-apply` → `smoke-health`.
  - Key variables
    - `RAYSERVICE_FILE`, `NAMESPACE`, `SERVICE_NAME`
  - Examples
  ```bash
  # Standard redeploy
  make redeploy

  # Custom namespace + manifest
  make redeploy NAMESPACE=staging RAYSERVICE_FILE=k8s/rayservice-staging.yaml
  ```

  ### redeploy-and-test / redeploy-and-test-ingress
  - What it does
    - `redeploy` then `quick-load-test-ingress` (ingress-only test).
  - Example
  ```bash
  make redeploy-and-test TEST_REQUESTS=100 TEST_CONCURRENCY=10
  ```

  ### redeploy-and-test-fallback
  - What it does
    - `redeploy` then `quick-load-test` with `USE_INGRESS_ONLY=false SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT=true`.
  - Example
  ```bash
  make redeploy-and-test-fallback TEST_REQUESTS=200 TEST_CONCURRENCY=20
  ```

  ### serve-status
  - What it does
    - Queries the Ray head pod to print Serve status (including `replica_states`).
  - Example
  ```bash
  make serve-status
  ```

  ### port-forward-dashboard / port-forward-dashboard-stop
  - What they do
    - Start/stop a background port-forward to the Ray dashboard (port 8265), with PID and log management.
  - Examples
  ```bash
  make port-forward-dashboard
  # open http://127.0.0.1:8265
  make port-forward-dashboard-stop
  ```


  ## Host header routing and manual checks

  Your ingress matches on the Host `embeddings.<ip>.nip.io`. Even when you hit the ingress by Node IP and port, you must send the Host header for routing.

  ### Quick curl checks
  ```bash
  # Substitute your NODE_IP and NODE_PORT if different
  NODE_IP=192.168.1.3
  NODE_PORT=30333
  HOST=embeddings.${NODE_IP//./-}.nip.io

  # Health via ingress (Host header required)
  curl -s -H "Host: $HOST" http://$NODE_IP:$NODE_PORT/health

  # Direct pod (bypasses ingress) — pick one IP from Serve endpoints
  POD_IP=$(kubectl get endpoints embedding-service-serve-svc -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}')
  curl -s http://$POD_IP:8000/health
  ```


  ## External proxy in front of ingress (optional)

  If you run an external NGINX proxy in front of Kubernetes ingress, preserve the Host header to match the ingress rule and forward to NodePort.

  ```nginx
  server {
    listen 80;
    server_name embeddings-proxy.local; # your proxy host

    client_max_body_size 20m;

    location / {
      # Upstream ingress
      proxy_pass http://192.168.1.3:30333;  # NODE_IP:NODE_PORT

      # Host header used by ingress routing
      proxy_set_header Host embeddings.192-168-1-3.nip.io;

      proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
      proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
      proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;

      proxy_http_version 1.1;
      proxy_set_header Connection "";
      proxy_buffering on;
      proxy_buffers 16 64k;
      proxy_buffer_size 64k;
      proxy_read_timeout 180s;
      proxy_send_timeout 180s;
      proxy_next_upstream error timeout http_500 http_502 http_503 http_504 invalid_header;
      proxy_next_upstream_tries 2;
    }
  }
  ```

  Tip: parameterize the upstream and Host if you deploy this across environments.


  ## Parameter quick reference by target

  | Target | Primary variables |
  |---|---|
  | build-and-push-optimized | REGISTRY, IMAGE_NAME, VERSION_FILE |
  | smoke-health | NODE_PORT, NAMESPACE, INGRESS_POST_FALLBACK_WAIT_SECS |
  | quick-load-test-ingress | TEST_REQUESTS, TEST_CONCURRENCY, TEST_SEGMENTATION |
  | quick-load-test | USE_INGRESS_ONLY, INGRESS_WAIT_SECS, SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT, TEST_* |
  | redeploy | RAYSERVICE_FILE, NAMESPACE, SERVICE_NAME |
  | redeploy-and-test(-ingress) | TEST_REQUESTS, TEST_CONCURRENCY |
  | redeploy-and-test-fallback | TEST_REQUESTS, TEST_CONCURRENCY (and uses USE_INGRESS_ONLY=false, SKIP_HEALTH_WAIT=true) |
  | serve-status | NAMESPACE |
  | port-forward-dashboard(-stop) | DASHBOARD_PORT (fixed in Makefile), NAMESPACE |


  ## CI/CD quick examples
